item.content:encoded:
We've got another exciting slate of NFL games for Week 8, headlined by a matchup between the Baltimore Ravens and Buffalo Bills. We've got eight games in the early window and three games in the afternoon.

Among the injuries we're watching ahead of kickoff: Patriots WR A.J. Brown is out with a knee injury after making his return from an ankle issue that landed him on IR earlier this season, while RB TreVeyon Henderson is out with an illness. Eagles WR DeVonta Smith is out with a hamstring issue. Jets RB Breece Hall will reportedly miss another game with a quad injury, and Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle is reportedly trending toward playing through a chest injury he aggravated last week.

On the positive front, injury-wise, the Ravens will see quarterback Lamar Jackson return from an ankle injury this week.

item.title: Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: Lineup advice for Week 8 from Justin Boone
item.description: Fantasy football analyst Justin Boone shares his lineup advice for every position.
item.content:encoded:
Make any day feel like Game Day with the Burger King Game Day Menu. Before you take your first bite, get your lineup ready with this week's must-starts and sits.

Justin Boone provides a weekly look at undervalued fantasy players to consider starting this week and potential busts you might want to leave on your bench.

For the rest of your lineup decisions, consult his Week 8 rankings.

Starts

Dak Prescott, QB, Cowboys

vs. Cardinals

Prescott is coming off a three-touchdown game that helped him finish as the QB6 overall last week. It was his first multiple-TD outing since Week 2. 

Now, he faces one of his easiest matchups of the season against a Cardinals defense allowing the third-most fantasy points to quarterbacks, including at least two touchdowns to the last six QBs they've faced. The Cowboys also have the highest implied team total on the week at 30.75, so you can expect another top-half QB1 finish from Prescott. 

Other QBs to start:

  • Jacoby Brissett at Cowboys – On the other side of that game, the Cowboys are giving up the eighth-most fantasy points to quarterbacks. Brissett is always risky, but his last matchup with an easy opponent resulted in a top-10 fantasy finish. I'm expecting something similar this time around. 

  • Kyler Murray at Lions – Murray is still getting comfortable in Kevin O'Connell's offense and a date with the Lions should help. Detroit is the most generous defense to fantasy QBs, with multiple TDs allowed to every quarterback its encountered, including at least three touchdowns to four of those six passers. Murray has also been more productive with his legs lately, which boosts his fantasy floor and ceiling. 

Rachaad White, RB, Commanders

vs. Eagles

Fantasy managers might not realize just how valuable White can be at the moment as a solid RB2 with Jacory Croskey-Merritt on IR. Prior to the Commanders' Week 7 bye, White handled nearly 70% of the snaps, coming away with 57 yards and a score. That's the third time in his last four outings where White has posted either 80-plus yards or a touchdown. While Washington is well rested after a week off, the Eagles — who are already banged up — will be playing on a short week after appearing on Monday Night Football. Philly's once-feared defense has lost its teeth, allowing some huge stat lines over the last month.

With Austin Ekeler and Jeremy McNichols only playing supporting roles, White is positioned to be a top-24 fantasy back in Week 8 and possibly longer.

Other RBs to start:

  • Bhayshul Tuten vs. Colts – Tuten has been remarkably consistent with his yardage totals this season, with at least 87 scrimmage yards in five of his six appearances. Coming off the bye week, Tuten and the Jags are 10-point favorites against a Colts team that just traded away defensive tackle DeForest Buckner and guard Quenton Nelson. Consider Tuten a borderline low-end RB1 this week. 

  • Jordan Mason at Lions – Aaron Jones Sr. is expected to play, but it's clear he's not 100% after battling through a knee injury recently. Mason handled 15 carries for 68 yards last week and should see the bulk of the touches yet again. In his only two appearances this year, Mason has racked up 127 yards and a touchdown on 30 carries.  

  • Blake Corum vs. Chargers – Corum has found the end zone in three straight games, while putting up at least 60 scrimmage yards in each of those contests. The Rams are 6.5-point favorites over a Chargers team that's permitting the ninth-most fantasy points to running backs. This is another spot where Corum can deliver top-24 RB production behind Kyren Williams. 

Michael Wilson, WR, Cardinals

at Cowboys

It might seem wild to have Wilson listed as a start after his disappointing performances the last three weeks since Marvin Harrison Jr. was removed from the picture. Wilson has been the WR52, WR56 and WR24 in weekly scoring, with stat lines of 4-30-0, 4-32-0 and 4-55-0 (with 11 rushing yards). He's also been held to eight targets or less in each of those games, after earning 30 targets the prior two weeks before Harrison's departure.

Now, Wilson gets a shootout with a Cowboys defense that's allowing the sixth-most fantasy points to his position. That makes him a viable fantasy WR2 this week. However, if you have Wilson, you should strongly consider moving him after this performance since he'll face the Seahawks, Rams and Chiefs the following three weeks.

Other WRs to start:

  • DJ Moore vs. Ravens – We've barely seen the DJ Moore experience this season, since he's only taken the field for 60% of the snaps in two contests due to injuries. In those two outings, Moore combined for 18 targets, 11 catches, 167 yards and a touchdown. The upside remains high with Moore expected to return, especially in a game tied for the highest projected point total on the week at 54.5.

  • Garrett Wilson vs. Raiders – Fantasy managers are down on Wilson after back-to-back quieter games, but let's not forget he was the WR12 after the first five weeks. Wilson voiced his displeasure with the recent reduced targets on the sideline during last week's loss to the Dolphins and it's setting up a squeaky-wheel situation. The Raiders have allowed double-digit fantasy points to six different receivers over the last month, and I'd expect Wilson to join that list.  

  • Stefon Diggs vs. Eagles – With Terry McLaurin out for the year, the Commanders' receiving corps is going to look a little different coming out of the bye. While Diggs' role might not change that much, he's likely to see more targets. That's notable against an Eagles defense that's giving up the second-most fantasy points to receivers, the sixth-most receiving yards and the ninth-most receiving touchdowns. In the last four games, six WRs have posted at least 70 yards against Philly.

Hunter Henry, TE, Patriots

at Dolphins

Henry has been a streaky fantasy player in the past, so I tend to not get too excited when he puts together three or four strong performances. We're currently in the midst of that kind of stretch with stat lines of 5-62-0, 3-44-1, 4-48-1 and 7-71-0 over the last month. Fortunately, this week he gets a Dolphins defense that's giving up the third-most fantasy points to tight ends. In its last five outings, Miami has allowed at least one touchdown to five different tight ends and the only game during that stretch where it didn't let a TE find the end zone, T.J. Hockenson hit them up for 13 catches and 119 yards. 

Henry is a solid fantasy TE1 once again and even someone you could consider as a flex option this week, especially with A.J. Brown out.

Other TEs to start:

  • T.J. Hockenson at Lions – Speaking of Hockenson, he's also a quality start this week against a Lions defense permitting the most fantasy points to tight ends. That includes 10 touchdowns given up to the position in six games. 

  • Brenton Strange vs. Colts – As I mentioned in this week's waiver wire article, Strange is averaging the sixth-most targets among tight ends over the last month and has posted three very usable stat lines of 7-95-0, 7-68-0 and 5-44-0. That includes two top-12 weekly fantasy finishes. Follow that volume into a game versus a spiraling Colts squad. 

Sits

Patrick Mahomes, QB, Chiefs

at Broncos

Mahomes is the featured quarterback to sit for the second straight week after the Seahawks caused him to finish in the single digits for fantasy points. After starting the season with two straight top-10 fantasy results, Mahomes hasn't cracked the QB1 range in his last four games (QB20, QB13, Q23, QB25). 

Injuries to his pass-catchers and offensive line have been part of the problem and are only amplified more in tougher matchups. The Broncos fit that description, especially with Pat Surtain II slated to return from his ankle injury. 

It's also worth noting, Mahomes isn't running as much coming off the ACL last season, as expected. After averaging over 30 rushing yards per contest in 2025, he's under 12 yards per game this year. 

Other QBs to sit:

  • Caleb Williams at Seahawks – Williams gets the unenviable draw of facing the Seahawks' stifling defense this week. Seattle has held opposing QBs to the second-fewest passing yards and fantasy points this season.

  • Bo Nix vs. Chiefs – Nix finally had a good fantasy day in Week 7, but it was mostly thanks to a fluky 62-yard TD run. I wouldn't expect much from him against a Chiefs defense giving up the third-fewest fantasy points to QBs, including Nix himself, who only managed 131 passing yards, one TD, one interception and two rushing yards in their Week 1 matchup. 

Omarion Hampton, RB, Chargers

at Rams

Hampton only topped six fantasy points once in the four games before the Chargers' Week 7 bye. We also watched as this backfield became a true three-man, hot-hand committee, with Kimani Vidal and Keaton Mitchell. 

It's possible Mike McDaniel and the coaching staff made adjustments during their time off and are ready to fix the long list of problems with this offense, but expecting that to happen against the Rams is a stretch. 

Sean McVay's crew are 6.5-point favorites and if the Chargers are trailing, that could limit Hampton's upside, since the routes run were split almost evenly in their last outing (Hampton 15, Vidal 13, Mitchell 12). I'm treating Hampton as a TD-or-bust RB3 until further notice. 

Other RBs to sit:

  • Quinshon Judkins at Steelers – Judkins returned from injury with his best stat line of the season, compiling 104 yards and two touchdowns against the Titans. Those were impressive totals considering he only played 53% of the snaps, while Dylan Sampson handled 46%. Sampson also ran more routes (15-9). It seems likely that Sampson being back will limit Judkins' pass-catching role, which pushes Judkins into more of a TD-or-bust RB3 range in a matchup on the road with a tougher Steelers defense. 

  • Rico Dowdle vs. Browns – Dowdle's 15-touch, 86-yard performance against the Saints needs to be graded on a curve since New Orleans plays a fast-paced style and allows the most fantasy points to RBs. That caused Dowdle's usual 10 touches to inflate to 15. Jaylen Warren remains the clear lead back in Pittsburgh, making Dowdle too volatile to start in fantasy most weeks.

  • J.K. Dobbins vs. Chiefs – In Jonah Coleman's first game off IR, the rookie turned the Broncos backfield into a three-man committee and led the way by playing almost 50% of the snaps. That left Dobbins and RJ Harvey to share the other 50%. Even with Harvey landing on IR with a knee injury over the weekend, Coleman has provided the most juice in his limited action, while Dobbins hasn't been very efficient with his touches. In a difficult matchup with the Chiefs, Dobbins is far too risky to trust in your lineup.

Rome Odunze, WR, Bears

at Seahawks

Though Odunze is a quality real-life receiver, his role in the Bears' passing attack isn't leading to major fantasy production. After slow starts, Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland have gotten back on track, but Odunze has yet to find the end zone and has only topped 55 yards on two occasions. 

Meanwhile, the Seahawks defense is giving up the fewest fantasy points to receivers and has only let two wideouts top 60 yards against them this season. 

It's always possible Odunze could make a big play and finish with a fine stat line; this just isn't the matchup I want to take a chance on. 

Other WRs to sit:

  • Jaylen Waddle vs. Chiefs – Waddle has been one of the biggest disappointments of the fantasy season and is expected to play through a chest injury. Denver's No. 1 receiver has only gone over 50 yards once in seven games and has just a single touchdown in a Broncos uniform. This week, he gets to deal with a Chiefs defense that's the second-worst matchup for fantasy WRs and held him to one catch for two yards in the opener. 

  • Xavier Worthy at Broncos – Worthy's big-play ability is always enticing, but as we saw last week, he fades in difficult matchups. The third-year wideout has never posted more than 25 yards against the Broncos and, to make matters worse, Patrick Surtain II is slated to return to the lineup. 

  • Josh Downs at Jaguars – Downs hasn't gone over 50 yards in any of his last four games and is still searching for his first touchdown of 2026. His only hope for future fantasy value would be a trade to a contender. 

Pat Freiermuth, TE, Steelers

vs. Browns

With injuries at the position and four teams on bye — including starting tight ends like George Kittle and Isaiah Likely — it's difficult to recommend sitting any tight end in the top 20. 

Freiermuth earns the mention as a potential sit, since he has yet to reach 50 yards in any game this season. He's also been held to 20 yards or less in three of his last four contests. Freiermuth is always a threat to score a touchdown and he did just that against the Browns back in Week 4. But if you're starting him this week, just know that without a TD, he's likely to let you down. 

Other TEs to sit:

  • Tyler Higbee vs. Chargers – After eclipsing 60 yards in three consecutive games, Higbee has fallen back to earth with stat lines of 4-22-0 and 2-14-0. The Chargers are the ninth-toughest matchup for fantasy tight ends, but that likely won't matter. The Rams will get up in this game and lean on the run. 

  • Mike Gesicki vs. Titans – Gesicki has scored five TDs this season, which has masked some very weak box scores otherwise. In the past two games, Gesicki's only catch in each outing was for a short touchdown. He managed just three targets during that span. That's the most TD-or-bust profile I've ever seen.

item.title: Jonathan Taylor trade rumors: Deal ‘more likely than not’, per report
item.description: Giants appear to have plenty of competition for star running back.
item.content:encoded:
The Indianapolis Colts are “more likely than not” to trade star running back Jonathan Taylor, according to an update from NFL insider Jordan Schultz.

The New York Giants are known to be one of the teams that has inquired about Taylor. Per Schultz, the Minnesota Vikings Denver Broncos, Cincinnati Bengals, and Green Bay Packers are also in the mix.

Taylor traveled with the Colts this weekend as they are on the road to face the Jacksonville Jaguars. If the Colts are serious about trading the 27-year-old, playing him would be a calculated risk.

The Giants like their backfield of Cam Skattebo, Tryone Tracy (on IR with a hamstring injury), Devin Singletary and Gregory Desrosiers. It has been clear since the offseason, though, that Harbaugh would love to have a top-tier bellcow back.

The Giants were interested in Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker in free agency, and No. 3 overall pick Jeremiyah Love in the 2026 NFL Draft.

The Colts are said to be using the Carolina Panthers 2022 trade of Christian McCaffrey to the San Francisco 49ers as a model. In that trade, the Panthers received, 2023 second-, third-, and fourth-round picks, and a 2024w fifth-round selection.

item.title: NFL betting, odds, lines: Betting trends to know for Week 8's biggest games
item.description: Here are a few betting trends to help you with your NFL wagers in Week 8.
item.content:encoded:
As the 2026-27 season nears its midpoint, a half-dozen teams are tied atop the NFL's point-spread standings. All are 5-2 ATS.

Flip those standings upside down and you'll find seven teams that have been anything but bettor friendly; each are 2-4-1 ATS or worse.

As fate would have it, my NFL betting trends report highlighting the five best matchups in Week 8 features four of the league's most profitable franchises, plus a pair of 4-2 ATS squads and three of the league's biggest money burners.

In all, I dug up multiple NFL betting trends for a trio of division rivalry battles, as well as a clash of perennial AFC contenders currently at opposite ends of the profitability spectrum. 

Capping things off is a Monday Night Football showdown pitting the hottest ATS team on the planet against an opponent that has stung bettors more often than not this season.

Vikings at Lions (-3.5, 46.5)

Moneyline: Vikings +145/Lions -175

• The Vikings emerged from their Week 6 bye and held off Indianapolis 16-10 on Sunday. Not only is Minnesota (6-0) the last undefeated team standing, but it has won 11 consecutive games since early December.

Despite failing to cover as 7-point home favorites against the Colts, the Vikings are still 8-2-1 ATS during their winning streak (4-2 ATS in 2026).

• The Lions entered their Week 6 bye off a 45-21 rout of Arizona as 5.5-point road favorites, then returned to work Sunday and nipped Green Bay 20-17 on a last-second field goal.

Detroit has posted consecutive victories for the first time since a four-game winning streak from Weeks 2-5 last season. However, after barely failing to cover the 3.5-point spread against the Packers, the Lions are now 1-4-1 ATS this year —  part of an ongoing 5-12-1 ATS drought.

• During its 11-game heater, Minnesota has taken down four division opponents (3-0-1 ATS). It also has won and covered five straight road contests and recorded outright upsets in three games as an underdog.

Conversely, during their 18-game spread-covering slump, the Lions sport these negative NFL betting trends: 2-6-1 ATS at home, 4-8-1 ATS as a favorite and 1-3 SU and ATS against the NFC North (0-3 SU and ATS when favored).

• The Vikings swept Detroit last year, scoring upsets both times. After eking out a 27-24 victory as 9.5-point underdogs in Week 9, they rolled 23-10 as a seven-point pup in Week 17.

Prior to notching its first season sweep of the Lions since 2020, Minnesota had lost five consecutive meetings in this rivalry and gone 0-9 ATS in the previous nine clashes.

• Detroit's first five games of the season flew over the total, with each reaching at least 55 points. Although that streak ended Sunday against the Packers, the over is still 13-5 in the last 18 at Ford Field. All 13 blew past 50 combined points.

On the flip side, Minnesota is on a 13-2 under stretch, including 6-1 on the road. Total points scored in the Vikings' last five games: 12, 39, 25, 36 and 26.

• While the over/under split in four Vikings-Lions battles the past two seasons, the over is still 8-4 in the last dozen head-to-head matchups.

Also, since 2019, the over is 6-1 when the Lions host. All six overs featured at least 50 combined points.

Ravens at Bills (-3.5, 54.5)

Moneyline: Ravens +150/Bills -175

• Baltimore is coming off a pair of AFC North setbacks, following a last-second 13-10 loss at Cleveland as a 3-point favorite with Sunday's 35-13 debacle against Cincinnati as a 3-point home underdog.

The Ravens — who have played the last 3½ games without injured starting quarterback Lamar Jackson — blew second-half leads of 10-0 to the Browns and 13-0 to the Bengals.

Since opening the season with a 41-23 rout of the Colts as a three-point chalk, Baltimore is 1-5 ATS. However, prior to last week, the Ravens had registered three straight upsets as underdogs.

• Buffalo took last week off after a successful two-game West Coast road trip that began with a 37-34 overtime upset of the Rams as a 3.5-point underdog and ended with a 33-30 win at the Raiders as 5.5-point favorites.

The Bills are off to a 5-1 SU and 4-2 ATS start, with all five wins coming against non-division opponents (4-1 ATS). 

• Buffalo dropped its most recent home game 29-26 to New England as a 7-point favorite. Still, since Week 15 of the 2021 season, the Bills have won 38 of 45 on their turf (including four of six in the postseason).

However, during this stretch of home dominance, Buffalo is only 24-21 ATS (6-4 ATS when laying less than six points).

• Including a thrilling 2024 AFC divisional playoff matchup, the Bills and Ravens have squared off four times since 2022. Buffalo won three of those contests — by margins of 3, 2 and 1 — while going 2-1-1 ATS.

The only lopsided meeting: Baltimore's 35-10 home win as a 2.5-point favorite in Week 4 of 2024.

• The last two Ravens-Bills clashes went over the total (27-25 in the 2024 playoffs; 41-40 in the 2025 season opener).

Three additional NFL betting trends explain why the total in this contest is sky high: The over is 9-2 in Buffalo's last 11 overall (5-1 this season), 5-2 in the Bills' last seven at home and 5-2 in Baltimore's last seven as a visitor.

Browns at Steelers (-3.5, 39.5)

Moneyline: Browns +160/Steelers -190

• Cleveland and Pittsburgh technically share first place in the AFC North, as both teams are 5-2 SU and ATS.

However, the Browns currently hold the tiebreaker by virtue of their 27-24 upset of the Steelers in Week 4 as 3-point home underdogs.

That's among a quartet of three-point victories that Cleveland has racked up in the last four weeks, with three of those wins secured on field goals in the final seconds. 

In addition to beating Pittsburgh at the gun, Browns kicker Andre Szmyt nailed game-winners that knocked off Baltimore in Week 6 (13-10) and Tennessee last week (27-24).

• Hours before Cleveland rallied to beat the Titans as 2-point road favorites, the Steelers outlasted New Orleans 16-10 in Paris, covering as 3-point favorites.

Pittsburgh has won and covered three in a row since falling at Cleveland, all as a favorite. In fact, aside from the loss to the Browns, the Steelers are 4-0 SU and ATS when laying points this season.

• Going back to Week 16 last year, the Browns are on a 7-3 SU and 8-2 ATS roll. Over these 10 contests, they're 6-3 SU and 7-2 ATS as an underdog (including two upsets of Pittsburgh).

Then again, the Steelers are 3-0 SU and ATS at home in 2026.

• Cleveland has now won and covered four of the last six against the Steelers. However, all four of those victories were in Ohio. Which leads to these eye-popping NFL betting trends:

The Browns have lost 31 of 33 regular-season games in Pittsburgh since 1990, including 23 in a row since 2004. Cleveland also has failed to cover the spread in eight straight visits to the Steel City — part of a 2-11-1 ATS funk in Pittsburgh since 2012.

Also worth noting: The straight-up winner has cashed in 15 of the last 16 meetings, including 11 in a row since 2021. 

• The Steelers have hurdled the total in four of their last five, including two straight at home. The over is also 3-1 in Cleveland's four road games this season.

However, the under has hit in five of seven Browns-Steelers battles in Pittsburgh since 2019.

Chiefs (-1.5, 40.5) at Broncos

Moneyline: Chiefs -120/Broncos +100

• After a 5-0 start to the season, Kansas City went to Seattle and got mauled in a 20-3 loss in the Week 7 Sunday Night Football game.

The Chiefs never threatened to cover as 3-point road underdogs, continuing this odd NFL betting trend: They've now alternated ATS wins and losses in nine consecutive games dating to Week 16 of last season.

• Denver is riding a three-game SU and ATS winning streak, the latest triumph being Sunday's 30-16 blowout of the Cardinals as 4.5-point road chalk.

The Broncos' defense has not surrendered more than 17 points during the three-game surge.

• Going back to the 2024 regular-season finale — a meaningless 38-0 loss at Denver — the Chiefs are 3-9 SU and 2-10 ATS away from Arrowhead Stadium.

During this stretch, Kansas City is 3-7 SU and 2-8 ATS as a road favorite.

• Kansas City kicked off this season with a 31-10 thrashing of the Broncos, easily cashing as a 2.5-point home favorite.

Even with that result, though, Denver has won four of the last six head-to-head and is 7-3 ATS in the last 10 (6-2 ATS as an underdog).

Additionally, the Broncos have won three straight regular-season games as a home underdog, including last year's 22-19 upset of the Chiefs as 4.5-point pups.

• The under has hit in seven consecutive meetings in this AFC West rivalry, including all three in the Mile High City.

Two of those seven contests topped out at 41 combined points (including the Week 1 tussle in K.C.). Otherwise, the two squads have not cleared 38 points since the Chiefs' 27-24 home win in Week 17 of 2022.

Furthermore, the under is 22-7 in the Chiefs' last 29 regular-season games, with 17 failing to eclipse 40 total points. The under is also 7-2 in Denver's last nine overall, only three of which hurdled 40 points.

Bears at Seahawks (-3, 46.5)

Moneyline: Bears +145/Seahawks -175

• Chicago kicked off the Week 7 slate with a 30-24 Thursday Night Football victory over the Patriots, cashing as a 3-point home favorite.

The Bears, who have scored at least 30 points in three of the four games that quarterback Caleb Williams has started, are now 5-2 SU and ATS. That includes a 5-0 SU and ATS mark against non-NFC North opponents.

• Seattle rebounded from consecutive narrow defeats — 32-29 to San Francisco at home and 17-14 at Denver in overtime — with a 20-3 dismantling of Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs on Sunday night.

The pivotal character in the Seahawks' story so far has been the defense: That unit has surrendered an average of 10.8 points in four victories and 27.3 points in three losses.

• Chicago joins the Browns, Steelers, Broncos, Giants and Raiders with an NFL-best 5-2 ATS mark.

What's more, no team has been more profitable than the Bears since the end of the 2024 campaign. Including two playoff contests, they're on ATS hot streaks of 20-7-1 overall, 9-3-1 on the road and 10-2-1 as an underdog. 

• On their way to winning Super Bowl 60, the Seahawks last year covered the spread in 15 of 20 games. However, they're just 2-4-1 ATS so far in 2026 (all as favorites).

One positive NFL betting trend working in Seattle's favor this week: Since the 2025 season began, Seattle is 17-3 SU and 14-5-1 ATS when favored by fewer than eight points (playoffs included).

• Looking for a reason to bet the over in this contest? Here you go: In the last 11 road games that Williams has been under center since the start of last season, the Bears and their opponents have combined for at least 49 points nine times.

Combined points in those 11 road outings: 73, 49, 49, 46, 89, 36, 49, 49, 80, 96 and 54.

item.title: 3 things to buy, 1 thing to sell for the Cowboys vs Cardinals
item.description: We’ve got your weekly Cowboys buy/sell report
item.content:encoded:
The Dallas Cowboys finally put together a complete offensive performance in Philadelphia, and now they will try to carry that momentum into their matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. Javonte Williams delivered a career night against the Eagles, CeeDee Lamb found the end zone twice, and the Cowboys’ rushing attack finally looked like the unit it was supposed to be at the start of the season.

The Cardinals have struggled defensively against the run, their offensive line is dealing with injuries, and the Cowboys are beginning to show some improvement against opposing rushing attacks. Concerns remain, particularly about Dallas’ tight end production and third-down defense.

Here are some buy/sells for Week 8.

Buy: Javonte Williams

After waiting six weeks for Dallas to give him a substantial workload, Javonte Williams finally showed what he can do when the coaching staff commits to the ground game. His career performance against Philadelphia should earn him another healthy workload against Arizona.

Williams rushed for 155 yards and a touchdown on 25 carries against the Eagles, averaging 6.2 yards per attempt. It was his best performance of the season and the most rushing yards by a Cowboys running back in nearly a decade. More importantly, it helped Dallas establish an offensive identity that had been missing during its consecutive losses to Tampa Bay and Green Bay.

Through seven games, Williams has recorded 472 rushing yards and eight touchdowns on 110 carries, averaging 4.3 yards per attempt with eight rushing touchdowns so far in 2026. Arizona should provide another favorable opportunity. The Cardinals have allowed 126.4 rushing yards per game, ranking 24th in the league.

Dallas finally showed what its offensive line can do when it moves downhill, and Williams should have opportunities to exploit that matchup. The biggest takeaway from Philadelphia was that Williams needs to be a focal point of this offense, not an afterthought. Schottenheimer should keep feeding him to achieve the balance he always talks about.

Buy: CeeDee Lamb

This is getting easy; this conversation comes up, and putting CeeDee Lamb in the mix is a no-brainer with how he’s performed so far this season. Lamb continues to remind everyone why he is the centerpiece of Dallas’ passing attack.

Against Philadelphia, Lamb caught five passes for 74 yards and two touchdowns, giving Prescott another dependable option in the red zone. Over seven games, Lamb has caught 53 passes for 651 yards and six touchdowns. He leads the Cowboys in receiving yards and has been one of the team’s most consistent offensive weapons throughout the season.

The Cardinals have struggled to consistently contain opposing offenses, and their secondary will have to account for both Lamb and George Pickens. That creates opportunities for Lamb to find favorable coverage, particularly if Dallas continues to establish Williams and force Arizona to respect the run.

Lamb has six touchdowns through seven games, and his yardage production, second only to Jaxon Smith-Njigba, has become a Cowboys staple as Dallas looks to build consistency. Expect him to remain a major part of the offensive game plan against Arizona.

Buy: The Cowboys’ run defense

This might be the most surprising buy of the week, but the Cowboys’ run defense deserves some credit for its recent improvement. It is far from a finished product, but after being gashed by Tampa Bay, Dallas has shown signs that it can finally, at the very least, slow down opposing rushing attacks.

The Cowboys allowed Tampa Bay 241 rushing yards in Week 5, a performance that exposed how vulnerable the defense can be against a physical ground game. Since then, however, Dallas has allowed just 57 rushing yards to Green Bay and 121 to Philadelphia. Yes, the Saquon Barkley injury did play a role here.

That averages 89 rushing yards allowed per game over the last two weeks, a significant improvement from the problems Dallas faced earlier in the season. The defensive front has started creating more disruption, and the return of key second-level contributors has helped the unit play with more consistency.

Arizona’s backfield presents an interesting test. Rookie Jeremiyah Love is expected to return after missing two games with an ankle injury, but the Cardinals will be without right guard Jon Gaines II, while center Hjalte Froholdt is questionable. Tyler Allgeier has also been dealing with a toe injury. Even with Love returning, the uncertainty along the offensive line could make it difficult for Arizona to establish the ground game, and Love hasn’t exactly set the world on fire when healthy.

If the defensive front controls the line of scrimmage and prevents Love from finding room to operate, it will force Jacoby Brissett to shoulder more of the offensive workload. The Cowboys have not suddenly become an elite run defense, but the last two games have been encouraging. Another decent performance against Arizona would go a long way toward showing that the improvement is real rather than a temporary stretch.

Sell: The Cowboys’ tight end position

Man, there was a time the tight end position in Dallas was a lock. Now the position has increasingly disappeared from Dallas’ passing attack, and it is becoming difficult to view the group as a difference-maker. Jake Ferguson’s production has fallen off sharply, while Brevyn Spann-Ford hasn’t received enough opportunities in the passing game to become a consistent contributor.

Ferguson has struggled to establish himself as any sort of contributor. Drops have been an issue, and against Philadelphia, Ferguson finished with no receptions on his lone target and played fewer than 56% of the offensive snaps for the second straight week.

Spann-Ford has seen more opportunities recently, including a season-high 52.9% snap share against Philadelphia. He caught both of his targets for 11 yards, but his overall production remains limited. Through seven games, he has recorded just nine receptions for 79 yards on 13 targets, leaving plenty to be desired from a position that was supposed to provide another reliable option for Prescott.

The Cowboys have talented receivers in Lamb and Pickens, and the emergence of Williams as a consistent rushing threat has helped diversify the offense. But the tight end position should still be contributing more than it has.

Whether it is Ferguson struggling to regain his confidence or Spann-Ford being used primarily as a blocker, Dallas is not getting much production from the group. For now, the Cowboys should continue leaning on their receivers and running backs while searching for more answers at tight end.

item.title: Vikings vs. Lions: Best odds, bets, and parlays
item.description: Minnesota Vikings vs. Detroit Lions Week 8 best player prop bets and parlays
item.content:encoded:
After a Week 7 victory in their first NFC North game of the season, the Detroit Lions host another divisional battle in Week 8. This time, the Lions host the top team in the NFC North, the undefeated Minnesota Vikings. Detroit is on a two-game winning streak, something they haven’t had since early Week 5 in 2025.

In my predictions last week, I went 1-2 in the top three bets, as the game was lower-scoring than expected, and tight end Sam LaPorta had a quiet performance on National Tight Ends Day. Quarterback Jared Goff did his job and got us back to .500.

With us back at even, it’s time to get back on the winning side on Sunday. The odds are with FanDuel Sportsbook.

1. Kyler Murray under 224.5 passing yards (-113)

Yes, I am trusting the Lions secondary here to slow down a quarterback. Safety Brian Branch is back at a full go after limited snaps last week, and it’s less about Detroit’s side and more about Minnesota’s struggles. Quarterback Kyler Murray hasn’t been the savior people expected at the position in this offense. He hasn’t had a good season so far, and this offense has been struggling mightily with him under center.

Murray is averaging 162.4 yards per game this season, with his best performance being against the Miami Dolphins, where he threw for 247 yards. In two of his five games this season, Murray has surpassed that mark, though he left Week 1 early with an injury.

In the first month of play, Detroit’s secondary averaged 304 passing yards per game. In their last two games, it was 267.5, and while that isn’t a big improvement, it’s a step in the right direction. Against a passing attack averaging 100 yards less than that, I think the Lions’ defense can meet it halfway and hold Murray to under 225 yards.

Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $18.85

2. Amon-Ra St. Brown alt receiving yards: 90+ (+142)

In his NFL career, St. Brown has 896 receiving yards against the Vikings over 10 games, averaging 89.6 yards per game. St. Brown is averaging 87.5 yards a game this season, so him hitting 90+ yards seems doable. Lions quarterback Jared Goff has been playing lights out, and his connection with St. Brown is still strong. St. Brown is coming off his best game of the season too, with 153 yards against the Green Bay Packers.

Sure, the Vikings defense is the toughest Detroit has played this season, but their coverage hasn’t been excellent, ranked 15th in coverage according to PFF. In their last three games, they’ve held opposing passing attacks to under 100 yards, but the offenses aren’t as explosive as the Lions. When they’ve played an offense with a tough passing attack, the Packers threw for 353 yards.

Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $24.40

3. Jared Goff alt passing yards: 250+ (-146)

As I stated in my last point, Goff is playing at an MVP level and was in his bag against the Packers. Minnesota will test Goff and the offensive line heavily with their high-blitzing defense, but Goff shouldn’t be afraid. He’s been the best quarterback in the NFL against the blitz, so Minnesota might want to ease up on that pressure.

Goff is averaging 298 yards per game, so getting 250 yards should be simple for him. If this game is low-scoring, it could come down to field goals. Goff can still hit the number if Detroit moves down the field but doesn’t find the end zone. The only threat to this bet is if Detroit gets up too much, and with Minnesota’s offense struggling, it might lean on the running game, which limits what Goff can do.

Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $16.76

If you want to turn these three single bets into a same-game parlay, the odds are +435 and $10 -> $53.55

Record: 9-9

Brandon’s Bold Bet

If you want to go bold and build a big parlay that could pay well, put these three bets together in a parlay:

  1. Anytime touchdown Jahmyr Gibbs (-270)
  2. Isaac TeSlaa over 18.5 receiving yards (-113)
  3. Jahmyr Gibbs over 4.5 receptions (+118)

Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs was held outside of the end zone for the first time this season. The last time that happened? Week 17 last season against… the Minnesota Vikings. Gibbs doesn’t like getting held out of the end zone, since he hasn’t had back-to-back games without touchdowns since 2023. I think Gibbs will want to not just score, but do better than he did last time he played the Vikings.

Wide receiver Isaac TeSlaa is averaging 32.8 yards per game, so asking him for 19 yards isn’t a lot. The last time he played the Vikings, he had three catches for 49 yards and a touchdown. With how heavy Minnesota will blitz, some receivers could be wide open quickly; TeSlaa could be an afterthought.

Going back to Gibbs, he’s only had one game this season where he didn’t get five catches; he got four against the Carolina Panthers. Gibbs is averaging six catches a game this season, so you should take advantage of the plus odds because it’s my favorite bet in this parlay.

Odds +395 and bet $10 -> $49.51

Record: 0-6

Do-it-all parlay

If you want to combine all six plays into a parlay and go big, here are the odds:

  1. Kyler Murray under 224.5 passing yards
  2. Amon-Ra St. Brown alt receiving yards: 90+
  3. Jared Goff alt passing yards: 250+
  4. Anytime touchdown Jahmyr Gibbs
  5. Isaac TeSlaa over 18.5 receiving yards
  6. Jahmyr Gibbs over 4.5 receptions

Odds +2597 and bet $10 -> $269.74

Record: 0-6

Use this information however you like. You can ignore it and watch the game, or, if you want to risk some money, follow these recommendations or test your own luck. Whatever you decide, please gamble responsibly and bet only money you can afford to lose.

item.title: Jets RB Braelon Allen set to start vs. Raiders while Breece Hall deals with quad injury: report
item.description: Braelon Allen is reportedly expected to start at running back for the Jets as Breece Hall continues to recover from a quad injury.
item.content:encoded:
The Jets are set to start Braelon Allen at running back while Breece Hall deals with his quad injury, according to a report Sunday morning by Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network.

New York is "hoping for next week" with Hall, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler subsequently reported.

"Hall practiced all week but on a limited basis, not quite there yet," Fowler wrote Sunday on X.

The Jets are at the Kansas City Chiefs for next Sunday's 1 p.m. kickoff.

New York listed Hall as questionable on Friday's injury report. He has not played for the Jets since Sept. 27, a 31-24 loss at the Detroit Lions in which his injury occurred.

Allen ran 17 times for 104 yards (6.1 average) in last Sunday's 28-25 loss to the Miami Dolphins. Through seven games this season, he has taken 91 carries for 418 yards (4.6 average) and two touchdowns.

"We have the best one-two combo in the NFL," New York offensive coordinator Frank Reich said last month in the wake of the Jets' 17-12 win over the Cleveland Browns.

"Braelon is outstanding. Really smart. Has the explosive runs, that was the big thing last week. We had four explosives in the game, tied for the most in the year for us. And a lot of that was his running."

Hall, who has missed the Jets' past four weeks, attempted 51 rushes for 163 yards (3.2 average) and one touchdown in the first three games.

item.title: Fantasy Football Rankings: Hayden Winks' RB Blueprint for Week 8
item.description: Fantasy football analyst Hayden Winks lays out the blueprint for the RB position in Week 8.
item.content:encoded:
The Blueprint is my weekly column and basically everything that I use to build out the most accurate rankings I can. There will be this RB column, a WR column and a combination column on the onesie positions. You will find film notes and endless charts. Maybe enough charts to stress test the Yahoo website. I kid.

It's impossible to get every ranking thoroughly early in the week, so be sure to keep checking in on these columns through Sunday morning. As always, my full rankings at every position are available.

1. Jahmyr Gibbs (vs. MIN) - 119.5 proj. total yards

Assuming he didn't sprain his ankle running out the clock last week, nothing has changed. Gibbs is inside the top 10 all time in RB fantasy points through six games.

A matchup with the Vikings will put that standing to the test. They've allowed the fewest fantasy points to RBs this season at just 14.5 half PPR points per game to entire backfields. Jonathan Taylor was able to spring lose for 110 total yards but that's been the exception with DC Brian Flores setting records with blitzes and crowding the line of scrimmage pre-snap. Gibbs was held to 5.4 and 4.3 half PPR points against them last year, respectively, while splitting time with David Montgomery. The Lions are projected for 24.75 points (ninth), far lower than usual.

2. Bijan Robinson (at TB) - 104.5 proj. total yards

Robinson has been a bit quieter recently with Michael Penix Jr. taking over at QB.

His receiving role has taken a big hit, while his rushing efficiency has scaled up. It's been about a wash on the averages, but the changes are worth tracking. He's the RB12 on RB16 usage this month. Brian Robinson missed last week, allowing Bijan to see 20 carries and five receptions.

Tampa Bay ranks 30th in half PPR points allowed per game to RBs (15.2), including 31st against RB rushing. Bijan has overcome the difficulties of the matchup before, finishing as the RB4, RB2 and RB7 in his last contests against them, respectively, with 106 total yards and a score in all. Atlanta is projected for 21.5 points (19th) as 2.5-point road underdogs.

3. Kenneth Walker III (at DEN) - 99.5 proj. total yards

Nobody runs on the Seahawks, even former Seahawk Super Bowl MVPs.

The Chiefs need to have at least one of their OTs and one of their top-two WRs to be threatening. Despite the flop, Walker is the RB2 on RB2 usage this season. Last week was the first time all year that he wasn't top-10 in both fantasy points and expected points.

The Broncos rank 11th in half PPR points allowed to RBs, giving up 14.5 rushing fantasy points per game (ninth). Walker lit them up for 191 total yards and two touchdowns in the season opener, forcing a truly ridiculous amount of missed tackles. Kansas City heads to Denver as 1.5-point road favorites with an implied total of 21.5 points (20th). He'll try to repeat that RB2 overall finish.

4. Javonte Williams (vs. ARI) - 94.5 proj. total yards

Williams comes off a career day on the ground, rushing 25 times for 155 yards and one score in Week 7. Over his last four contests, he sits as half PPR's RB5 on RB6 usage, producing six rushing scores in that span. He has handled nine carries inside the 5-yard line across these four weeks, turning five of them into short scores. That's the benefit of a healthy Cowboys OL.

Arizona has allowed the 10th-most half PPR points to opposing backfields (20.5 per game). The Cardinals gave up an RB1 finish to Jahmyr Gibbs in Week 5, an RB14 showing to Blake Corum in Week 6 and allowed all Broncos RBs to put up fantasy points. Dallas enters as 6.5-point home favorites with a week-high 30.5-point implied team total (first). That's simply too big to fail.

5. James Cook III (vs. BAL) - 99.5 proj. total yards

Nothing has really changed with Cook. He's the RB2 in rush YPG (104.5), while being the RB40 in receptions per game (1.7). In this elite offense, it's sustainable and comes with countless TDs. We can keep rinse-repeating this RB6 on RB11 pace for as long as the OL and Josh Allen are healthy.

The Ravens defense has allowed the fifth-fewest half PPR points to opposing RBs at 16.4 per game. They've allowed the fewest points in the air to RBs, while being 18th on the ground, where Cook does his damage. Bijan Robinson had 118 scoreless yards against them back in Week 5, while lesser talents were kept out of the top-24 overall this month. Buffalo enters as 3.5-point home favorites with a 28.5-point implied team total (second), and that's the real stat we should care about. The Bills dictate terms — opposing defenses are just holding on for dear life. It'll be great if Lamar Jackson is out there, too.

6. Derrick Henry (at BUF) - 89.5 proj. total yards

The splits with and without Lamar Jackson speak for themselves. The only other thing to take into account is the loss of first-round G/C Vega Ioane, who was a star early in the year.

Buffalo ranks third in half PPR points allowed to opposing RBs (24.5), having surrendered big recent days to Kyren Williams (RB8) and Ashton Jeanty (RB10). Baltimore heads in as 3.5-point road underdogs with an implied total of 25.0 points (eighth). The markets seem to think Lamar is going to play, as he returned to practice this week.

7. Chase Brown (vs. TEN) - 79.5 proj. total yards

Update: I've gone back and forth on Brown all week, and my official stance is to put on my "Fell For It Again" badge. I'm buying low. I just traded for Brown in the league I care most about.

Brown is still seeing 75% of the expected points in the backfield and is attached to an offense that's balling. Their OL is the best it's ever been, and eventually positive regression is coming. The Bengals have 15 passing TDs (third) to just three rushing TDs (31st), and there's no reason the gap should be that wide. Brown is still averaging 4.7 receptions per game in the most pass-heavy offense in neutral situations, so it really is about scoring in the red zone and ripping off the occasional explosive. The touchdown risk with Samaje Perine subbing in at the goal line last week is more than made up by the fact the Bengals have a 28.25-point team total.

The Titans rank 13th in fantasy points allowed to opposing running backs at 20.3 half PPR points per game, but they have shown stark splits. Tennessee sits eighth in points allowed to RB rushing while ranking 27th against RB receiving, allowing just 4.9 points per game through the air. Cincinnati enters with the league's highest neutral pass rate at 65% (first), but Brown's receiving upside is when Cincy is trailing. The Bengals are 10-point home favorites with an implied team total of 28.25 points (third). Hopefully things even out with red-zone scores. The team total is certainly on his side.

8. Braelon Allen (vs. LV)

Breece Hall (quad) was limited in practice all week and is in trade talks, so he’s getting another week off. It’ll be Allen as the clear cut starter. He’s averaged 13.4 half PPR points on 13.7 expected points, even including a game where the Jets ran the fourth-fewest plays in NFL history. Those are low-end RB1 numbers during bye weeks.

The Raiders aren’t a team to be threatened by either. They’ve allowed the fifth-most points to fantasy RBs this year, and three-of-four recent starters have cleared 121 total yards with a score. The Jets have a strong 24.0-point team total, and coach Aaron Glenn’s job is on the line at home.

9. Chuba Hubbard (at GB) - 89.5 proj. total yards

Hubbard had season lows in half PPR points (8.0) and expected points (9.0) with the Bucs destroying each side of the ball in the trenches. They have inexperienced first-rounder Monroe Freeling to step in for RT Taylor Moton (IR), but the entire unit needs to play better. The good news is they had for most of the season, allowing Hubbard to start out as the RB10 on RB15 usage. I haven't seen a single Jonathon Brooks report in a month, so Hubbard's upside RB2 value looks pretty baked in. We're just hoping Bryce Young doesn't turn back into a pumpkin this Halloween season.

The Packers rank sixth in half PPR points allowed to RBs at 23.3 per game, including 16.9 rushing points allowed per game (fourth). That has included a couple of outings against Jahmyr Gibbs, to be fair, but Javonte Williams (RB17) and D'Andre Swift (RB12) were both rock-solid this month against them. Green Bay is also down a pair of LBs if Zaire Franklin misses another game, and Micah Parsons isn't expected to play yet either. The Panthers travel on a short week as 3.5-point road underdogs with a 22-point implied team total (15th).

10. Rhamondre Stevenson (at MIA) - 89.5 proj. total yards

Update: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) was ruled out early, leaving Stevenson as the clear starter with Corey Kiner mixing in on early downs as a fellow bruiser type. In five games without him since 2025, Stevenson is the RB11 on RB15 usage on a per-game basis, averaging 14.7 half PPR points on 15.6 carries and 4.0 targets. Kiner is mixing in a bit more than he was during other parts of this split, but the Dolphins aren't a threat. Both can get home.

Miami ranks fourth in half PPR points allowed to opposing backfields at 23.7 points per game. The Dolphins have been especially vulnerable to pass-catching backs, allowing the most receiving fantasy points per game to RBs while sitting 17th against the run. For what it's worth, Stevenson dropped 34.3 half PPR points in Week 18 (RB1) and 18.7 points in Week 2 (RB6) against the Dolphins last year. New England enters as 7.5-point road favorites sporting a 26.0-point implied team total (fifth).

11. Kyren Williams (vs. LAC) - 89.5 proj. total yards

Williams sits as the RB6 in half PPR points per game (18.4) on RB2 usage (18.7 expected half PPR) over his last four contests. He leads all running backs with 7.3 targets per game over that window while playing in an offense that ranks third in neutral pass rate (63%). The career-best receiving usage has been more than enough to offset Blake Corum emerging. Corum had his season-best usage last week without Davante Adams, and Williams still finished as the RB12 on RB25 usage. It's simply a drive-by-drive rotation with Williams starting each half. His drives need to be the long ones to reach a ceiling.

The Chargers rank ninth in half PPR points allowed to RBs (21.6), surrendering recent top finishes to Kenneth Walker (RB1), J.K. Dobbins (RB16), Emanuel Wilson (RB6) and James Cook (RB6). The Landlord Rams enter as 6.5-point "home" favorites over their tenants, with a 25.5-point implied total (seventh).

12. Bucky Irving (vs. ATL) - 84 proj. total yards

Wow. The Bucs ran all over a sorry Panthers defense. Their OL was dominant, and Irving made the most of it. He handled a season-high 24 carries for 106 rushing yards and two touchdowns, leading to an RB2 finish on RB4 usage. Because everything worked, Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker got home in Baker Mayfield's return. This offense should be balanced while Mayfield's thumb heals, and Irving is in line for upside RB2 value. He's the RB14 on RB13 usage this season despite a month of problems at QB.

The Falcons have allowed the eighth-most half PPR points per game to RBs this year, particularly struggling in the receiving game (fourth most). Christian McCaffrey was the latest example of that, but D'Andre Swift (RB5), Derrick Henry (RB5) and Alvin Kamara (RB10) have made it a 4-game streak of allowing a top-10 fantasy finish. Tampa Bay enters as 2.5-point home favorites with an implied team total of 24.5 points (11th). This is a massive game for them.

13. Bhayshul Tuten (vs. IND) - 89.5 proj. total yards

Tuten is a post-bye riser after passing the pre-bye test on the ground. The Jaguars OL is worrisome, and Tuten is squeezed in some of the high-value touch areas; Chris Rodriguez Jr. will vulture TDs on occasion and LeQuint Allen plays obvious passing downs. But Tuten can still eat into those areas, because he's earned it. Over the past four games, Tuten is the RB17 on RB17 usage and 16.5 carries per game. That's probably closer to his floor than ceiling while he's fully healthy. Get ready for more spike weeks in the near term.

This is a great spot for Tuten, too. The Jaguars project for 28.0 points (fourth) against the Colts, who traded their best linemen on both sides of the ball. This defense is straight up a joke. They were blown off the ball on Jordan Mason carries last week, and Tuten can take them the distance like Jaylen Warren did in Week 5, when he was the RB2 overall.

14. Josh Jacobs (vs. CAR) - 79.5 proj. total yards

Jacobs was the RB11 on RB5 usage in his 2026 debut, while splitting the early-down rushing work with MarShawn Lloyd and posting far more receiving work (5-55-1) than he typically does. He had a highlight broken tackle on the sideline and looked like the best back on the team by far. We'll see if Lloyd can keep this split role long term, but in general, swapping five carries for five receptions is elite business in fantasy football.

The Packers won't have the OL that Jacobs benefited from in years past as a sure-fire top-10 fantasy back, but they're competitive on both sides of the ball and game scripts should generally be favorable. A repeat of last year's RB12 per-game finish sounds about right. I'd draft him in Round 3 right now and don't believe the Police Department will leak the evidence after being sued by Jacobs and the victim. That said, the NFL did not fine Jacobs or announce their "suspension," a signal that their investigation is ongoing while that last non-criminal court case is open.

The Panthers present a vulnerable spot on the ground, allowing 26.7 half PPR points per game to opposing backfields (second most). Carolina ranks first in half PPR points allowed to RB rushing with 21.7 per game, though they sit 26th against RB receiving. Bucky Irving (RB2) just turned 24 carries into 106 yards and two touchdowns against them in Week 7. Green Bay enters as 3.5-point home favorites with an implied team total of 25.5 points (sixth).

15. Ashton Jeanty (at NYJ) - 79.5 proj. total yards

Update: Jets DT D’Vondre Sweat is out:

T’Vondre Sweat splits

On field:

3.54 ypc
37.4% offensive rushing success rate

Off field:

4.87 ypc
48.9% offensive rushing success rate https://t.co/wsnOXY3oIN

— Ted Nguyen (@FB_FilmAnalysis) October 31, 2026

Jeanty's rushing volume has contracted lately, averaging 10.8 carries (RB36) and 30.5 rushing yards (RB47) over his last four games, but his passing-game involvement keeps him afloat. Over that 4-game stretch, he is the RB21 on RB13 usage, powered by 7.0 targets (RB2) and 5.3 receptions per game (RB3). In Week 7, he set season highs with eight receptions and 28 air yards, pulling in a 15-yard touchdown reception. The receiving role is clearly by design, while Klint Kubiak seems to be okay riding the hot hand on the ground.

Most of Jeanty's failures on the ground are because the C Tyler Linderbaum signing has Baum-ed, but he's still a bit slow to react and burst upfield, too. In the open field, his ankle seems fine, but Jeanty just never gets there. I don't think he's a great wide zone fit, and it was embarrassing that the Raiders couldn't run the ball when the Rams showed up with six+ DBs for a record amount of snaps last week. They basically started a S at off-ball LB, and the Raiders came up empty. SHEESH.

The Jets rank 15th in half PPR points allowed to running backs at 19.7 per game. New York surrendered an RB4 finish to Kyle Monangai in Week 4 and an RB14 outing to Ollie Gordon in Week 7. Neither are receiving-based backs, for what it's worth, but there's no way to call this anything other than a promising matchup. Las Vegas has an implied team total of 22.0 points (17th) as slight road dogs. The bigger issue is the Jets can play a slow-paced, run-first style on offense and the Raiders' own defense isn't getting off the field.

16. D'Andre Swift (at SEA) - 89.5 proj. total yards

Update: Kyle Monangai (turf toe) was ruled out. In Week 7's Thursday Night Football game after Roschon Johnson had fumbled the week prior, Swift finished as the RB13 on RB10 usage, touching the rock 26 total times. He does not look fully healthy, but this was nearly a bye with this game going from Thursday to the next Monday. I don't think the staff will want to use Johnson that much given the quality of the opponent and the importance of this matchup in the NFC Standings.

Unfortunately, a matchup with the Seahawks means a matchup with the only truly elite rushing defense out. They're in a league of their own in EPA per carry and success rate allowed on carries dating back to last year. In 2026, Seattle is allowing the fewest passing yards per game (158) and sixth-fewest rushing yards per game (89) and they're fairly healthy right now. They just shut Kenneth Walker III down to 57 total scoreless yards on Sunday Night Football as their Mona Lisa. The Bears head on the road as 3-point road underdogs with an implied total of 21.75 points (18th). Adjustments are needed.

17. Jaylen Warren (vs. CLE) - 89.5 proj. total yards

Warren has between 9.2 and 15.1 expected half PPR points in all seven games this year, and he's held the line even with Rico Dowdle returning over the past two weeks (RB17 and RB16 usage). Warren had 18 carries and three receptions in a French win last week with Dowdle sprinkling in for a third of the role throughout the game. The Steelers' MVP has handled 62% of the carries with Dowdle back, up from 48% in Weeks 1-3. Warren's floor is also held up by 3.4 receptions per game, in an offense that is fourth in neutral pass rate (60%) in the four Dowdle games.

The Browns rank 24th in half PPR points allowed to RBs (17.5 PG). Perhaps because of their speedy LB duo, Cleveland has been stout through the air, ranking 29th against RB receiving with 3.9 half PPR points allowed per game, but they sit 15th against RB rushing. Tony Pollard (RB1 overall) broke loose against them for 129 rushing yards and three scores in Week 7, while Braelon Allen (RB6) reached 116 rushing yards in Week 5. Warren himself had 126 scoreless yards in a Turf Monster game back in Week 4. Pittsburgh is listed as 3.5-point home favorites with an implied team total of 21.5 points (21st).

18. Jonathan Taylor (at JAX) - 69.5 proj. total yards

Taylor's 11.8 expected half PPR points last week (RB24) were his fewest since Week 9 of last year, if we remove his partial Week 18 game. The culprits were more Seth McGowen than normal, a bad offense and a bad matchup. Taylor is so good that he still finished with 18.0 half PPR points on 18 carries, but the margins are getting thinner within the confines of these spreadsheets. He's the RB9 on RB6 usage this month without Alec Pierce clearing space for the offense.

Now, he'll be without the best guard in the NFL after the Colts traded away Quenton Nelson. Right now, the Colts are fourth in PFF run-blocking grade at OG. That won't hold up now. McGowen is a sharp bench stash for 12-team leagues as we approach November 10. Taylor easily could be next.

Jacksonville ranks 31st against fantasy RBs, giving up just 14.6 half PPR points per game overall and an NFL-low 8.2 points per game on the ground (32nd). Offenses facing them have run the ball in neutral situations at the lowest rate (38%), too. The Colts don't have another way to move the ball consistently, so they may go down swinging anyways. A 19.5-point team total (23rd) for the Colts is less than ideal.

19. Tony Pollard (at CIN) - 79.5 proj. total yards

Without Tyjae Spears in Week 7, Pollard had a season-high 35.0 half PPR points (RB1 overall) on RB3 usage (21.9 expected points). He broke countless tackles against the Browns, scoring twice on his own doing, one on a safety split up the middle and another pitch to the outside where he took on a collision at the goal line. It was an impressive outing, and Pollard added three receptions to round out his fantasy spike week. That brings Pollard up to the RB18 on RB17 usage and RB12 carries per game.

It's slightly helpful that Spears missed that game, but the real reason for excess usage was that the game was close. Spears has been an afterthought to this staff. It's hard to believe the Titans will play many close games moving forward. Pollard is an RB3/FLEX, as he hadn't cleared 12.0 half PPR points all season prior to Week 7.

The matchup is absolutely a pain. The Bengals are a totally different team with star DT Dexter Lawrence and EDGE Boye Mafe up front. They're the best defense against the run this year and have allowed the fourth-fewest fantasy points to RBs. They stopped Derrick Henry last week (RB43) as the most recent example. If there's a way to beat them, it's using RBs as pass catchers to get them matched with Cincy's terrible LB duo. The Titans swim uphill with a 18.25-point team total.

20. Jeremiyah Love (at DAL) - 59.5 proj. total yards

Update: Love was a full participant on Friday.

Love is hopefully healed from both of his ankle sprains after taking two weeks off, and I will say that he was leaping over defenders in Week 5 after suffering both of them. He's a freak athlete, and the hope is the Cardinals were being precautionary so they can get the best version of him to wind down the year.

It's best to throw out a lot of his season when trying to project forward. There were too many injured games and an outing against the Seahawks to try to tangle with. What I did notice was Bam freaking Knight having RB12 and RB18 usage over the past two weeks while Tyler Allgeier was kept in what coach Matt LaFleur calls a "complementary role." It's possible Knight is a short-term thorn in his side, but Allgeier being the one to prevent Love being a fantasy RB2 is not likely at this point. We'll wait for better news later on to decide where in RB2 Land Love belongs.

Dallas enters Week 8 ranked seventh in half PPR points allowed to RBs at 22.6 points per game. While they sit 15th in receiving points allowed to the position, the Cowboys have surrendered the fifth-most rushing points per game to opposing backfields. Opponents have attacked them relentlessly on the ground, as Dallas has faced a 44% neutral pass rate (lowest in the league). Bucky Irving delivered 30.5 half PPR points (RB3) against them in Week 5, while Saquon Barkley posted 14.1 points (RB20) in Week 7 on 10 dang snaps. Arizona travels as 6.5-point road underdogs with an implied team total of 23.75 points (12th).

21. Ollie Gordon II (vs. NE) - 79.5 proj. total yards

Gordon has been a focal point of Miami's offense, checking in as the RB13 in half PPR points per game on RB9 usage over his last four contests. He has averaged 15.4 half PPR points on 16.0 expected points per game, scoring a touchdown in each outing. His workload climbed to season highs of 25 carries and 103 rushing yards in Week 7 against the Jets, backed by five carries inside the 5-yard line. Targets remain scarce at 2.0 per game, but his heavy workload, a fancy staple of run plays by OC Bobby Slowik and an underrated OL are enough to trust.

The Patriots rank 18th in half PPR points allowed to opposing backfields at 18.4 points per game. Miami leans heavily into the ground game in balanced scripts, ranking 31st in neutral pass rate at 43%, but that does mean running into the teeth of opponent defenses. The Dolphins are 7.5-point home underdogs with an implied team total of 18.5 points (25th). That's the same range of points that Gordon has overcome as the starter.

22. Saquon Barkley (at WAS) - 69.5 proj. total yards

Barkley went DNP-DNP-limited in practice but was left without an injury designation. He said his back flared up on the first run last week, and the way trainers were working on him, that appears to be the truth. This week, Barkley said the back and hamstring injuries are ones he’ll have to manage during Week 8:

Saquon Barkley said his back and hamstring injuries are ones he'll have to manage during the game if he's cleared to play against the Commanders.

I asked him how he weighs "gutting it out" knowing that a team that needs a win needs him + the risk of aggravating a short-term…

— Brooks Kubena (@BKubena) October 30, 2026

It’s fair to lower his median and floor projections given the uncertainty, fully aware that his ceiling might even be higher in games with Tanner McKee than Jalen Hurts for rushing-related reasons. Barkley is a boom-bust RB2 with a neutral matchup. Barkley historically has sonned the Commanders, but they have a new DC and scheme that has been fairly effective. They held Barkley to 80 scoreless yards in Week 1 before the team fully fell apart. Against all backs, Washington has allowed the seventh-fewest points and has flooded the line of scrimmage with potential blitzers. Philly has a 17.0-point team total.

23. Rachaad White (vs. PHI) - 59.5 proj. total yards

Off the bye, White has some sleeper RB3/FLEX appeal with Bill Croskey-Merritt on IR. White had a season-high 13.7 half PPR points (RB11) on RB22 usage before the week off, and his lone competition is Austin Ekeler and thumper Jeremy McNichols. White will mix in at the goal line and should be the starter for the next month, but we're really here for the PPR scam. He's averaged 3.0 receptions per game (RB17) this month.

Philadelphia ranks 16th in half PPR points allowed to opposing backfields at 19.6 per game. The Eagles have been stingy through the air to backs, allowing just 3.6 half PPR points per game to RB receiving (30th) compared to 16.0 points on RB rushes (seventh most). That doesn't necessarily work in White's favor, but the fact the Eagles were run out of the building on Monday Night Football is still promising for what typically is a brutal matchup. Washington is listed as 4.5-point home favorites with an implied total of 22.5 points (14th).

24. Jonah Coleman (vs. KC) - 69.5 proj. total yards

Update: RJ Harvey (knee) was ruled out after a practice injury. That's exactly the type of thing that could send Coleman into a fringe RB2 role if he can distance himself from Dobbins. He was behind Dobbins to start last week while splitting time with Harvey on passing downs. Coleman should handle most of the passing downs now, and Coleman also closed out the game while up multiple scores. Dobbins is probably the starter in a two-back committee, but Coleman has the "it can be a boat" advantage.

Unfortunately, the Broncos only project for 19.5 points against the Chiefs. They've only allowed 17.1 half PPR points per game to opposing backfields.

25. Quinshon Judkins (at PIT) - 54.5 proj. total yards

Judkins had his best game of the year (RB3 on RB22 usage), right as RB2 Dylan Sampson returned from injury. Judkins scored twice, once from distance and once inside the 10-yard line. Judkins ran with burst and particularly had success running behind top-10 rookie pick LT Spencer Fano, who switched sides this offseason. This OL could gel more after that Week 6 bye, and Judkins stands to benefit most.

That said, Judkins' snaps and receiving role took a hit with Sampson back. He simply won't maintain the three+ reception average (RB12) he had in Weeks 1-5 without him, so I'd view his current RB19 on RB16 standing as closer to his ceiling than baseline. The Browns will also run Deshaun Watson in short yardage and sprinkle in KC Concepcion carries, too. The good news is Judkins' tape and the OL's tape seemed to be the best they've been all year.

26. Blake Corum (vs. LAC) - 59.5 proj. total yards

Corum has been the RB15, RB14 and RB15 in his last three games. He set a new season high with 14.0 expected half PPR points (RB15) without Davante Adams, while rotating drives with Kyren Williams as usual. The Rams will flirt with record usage of 3-TE sets moving forward, and they may run more in the red zone, helping Corum on the margins. As usual, Corum is best when the Rams are up on the scoreboard, as Williams is far more involved as a receiver while trailing.

The Chargers rank ninth in half PPR points allowed to opposing running backs at 21.6 points per game, though they are much friendlier on the ground (sixth most points allowed) than through the air (25th). Opposing lead backs have capitalized recently, including Kenneth Walker III (RB1) and Emanuel Wilson (RB6). The Rams feature a 63% neutral pass rate (third), and they are 6.5-point home favorites with an implied total of 25.5 points (seventh).

27. Jordan Mason (at DET) - 54.5 proj. total yards

Update: Mason was the RB28 in expected half PPR points coming off his finger injury last week and was the RB23 in usage in Week 1. Both games included a drive-by-drive rotation, led by Aaron Jones Sr., who had another blow to his nagging knee injury last week. We'll see how he fares in practice this week. For now, Mason is a FLEX-only play as a worse version of the Kyle Monangai or Blake Corum role. Better play from Kyler Murray would go a long way for Mason's fantasy hopes.

The Vikings have a 21.75-point team total against the Lions, as 3-point road dogs. The Lions have been more of a pass funnel on defense this year, but Josh Jacobs (RB11) and Chuba Hubbard (RB7) both had nice outings against them this month in similar roles.

28. Jadarian Price (vs. CHI)

Price is back from injured reserve with full participations in back-to-back practices. He had a chest injury and should be himself now that he’s cleared to play. The Seahawks have to activate him by Monday, but Seahawks reporters believe he will be active for MNF. Ditto for Zach Charbonnet, who also had a full participation in practice. There is typically a big ramp up period for running backs who are playing their first games after nine months of ACL rehab.

It’s unclear how this backfield will be split with Emanuel Wilson threatening in short yardage and George Holani available for passing downs. I’d guess one of those two are healthy scratched, and Price is the starter. That was the case earlier on before Wilson was enjoying an RB14 on RB24 usage month on 19.75 carries per game (RB5) without Price.

Here’s what I wrote ahead of Week 3 when Price had his setback:

“Through two weeks, Price is the RB31 on RB27 usage, which is very similar to the Kenneth Walker split in the regular season when Zach Charbonnet was stealing the high-value opportunities. Last week, Price started each half and ended with 11.7 expected half PPR points. He fumbled in a big pile in the 2nd quarter but wasn't directly benched. Emmanuel Wilson played in each half and handled most of the short-yardage and goal-line work, while George Holani played the obvious pass-down snaps. Price picked up a chest injury in the second half, so it was largely Wilson in "run out the clock" mode. At the very end of the game TE A.J. Barner scored on a Tush Push, too.”

In terms of the matchup, it’s a fine one. Quenton Nelson and Jeffery Simmons are largely a net wash, and then the rest of the Bears defensive front isn’t too intimidating. They’ve been holding opposing fantasy RBs this year, but there have been some weak opponents and weird game scripts that have played into that. The Seahawks have a 24.75-point team total (10th) as three-point favorites at home. That’s fantasy RB game script.

29. Rico Dowdle (vs. CLE) - 39.5 proj. total yards

Dowdle ranks as the RB50 in half PPR points per game on RB36 expected points across his four appearances this season. He set season highs across the board in Week 7 against New Orleans, logging 11.6 half PPR points on 12.6 expected points while catching all six of his targets for 45 yards alongside nine carries for 41 yards. His target involvement has climbed across each of his last three active games, rising from two targets in Week 2 to four in Week 6 and six in Week 7, producing a baseline of 3.3 receptions per game (13th).

Cleveland ranks 24th in half PPR points allowed to opposing running backs at 17.5 per game. The Browns allow only 3.9 half PPR points per game to RB receiving (29th), funneling the majority of backfield damage to the ground where they rank 15th with 13.5 points allowed per game. However, opposing starters Tony Pollard (RB1) and Braelon Allen (RB6) each found the end zone against them over the past three weeks. Pittsburgh sits as 3.5-point home favorites with an implied team total of 21.5 points (21st).

30. Aaron Jones (at DET) - 39.5 proj. total yards

Update: Jones (knee) was able to get in a full practice on Friday with a lingering MCL injury popping up just about every week. Mason may not start the game, but if they can, the Vikings will want to off-load Jones' snaps to Mason while he's fresh off his own absence. Last week, Jones was the RB42 in usage. The Vikings have a 21.75-point team total against the Lions, as 3-point road dogs.

31. J.K. Dobbins (vs. KC) - 39.5 proj. total yards

Update: RJ Harvey (knee) was ruled out so this could be back to a two-back committee. Dobbins will have a chunk of the early-down role, while Coleman can mix in there in addition to playing most of the passing-down snaps.

The Broncos are in 3-RB committee hell right now, with rookie Jonah Coleman emerging from IR with a real role. Dobbins was the starter, played well on tape and converted the backfield's lone inside the 5-yard line opportunity, but he only had 4.8 expected half PPR points in a positive game script because Coleman stole the second half. Through three quarters, snaps were Coleman (15), Dobbins (13) and RJ Harvey (12). If Dobbins doesn't run well early, he'll lose the veteran nod in a battle for the hot hand. Without any late-down snaps last week and minimal receiving work to fall back on, Dobbins can't be started in fantasy, even if the Broncos are running the ball more with Sean Payton back on the sticks.

The Chiefs have a strong defense, allowing the 25th-most fantasy points to RBs this year (though the schedule has been light). Offenses facing them have the second-lowest neutral pass rate (47%) to keep DC Steve Spagnuolo from exotic-ing them into bad moments, but it puts a lid on the total ceiling of the offense. Denver faces them as 1.5-point home underdogs carrying a 20.0-point implied team total (22nd). Dobbins had 36 scoreless yards against them in Week 1's flop.

32. Omarion Hampton (at LAR) - 39.5 proj. total yards

Hampton is the RB47 in half PPR points per game on RB35 usage over his last four games, averaging 11.3 carries and 38 rushing yards. He lost snaps to Kimani Vidal for his pass protection, and I totally get it. Hampton is simply not a great fit for the wide zone that OC Mike McDaniel wants to run. It's possible the bye week was enough to figure things out with Hampton, but that's the only hope at this point. He's a dart-throw FLEX.

The Rams rank 21st against fantasy RBs, yielding 17.7 half PPR points per game. Los Angeles has been vulnerable to running backs through the air, ranking fifth in receiving points allowed to the position compared to 28th against the run. The Chargers also run a league-low 38% neutral pass rate (32nd). Los Angeles enters as 6.5-point road underdogs with a 19.5-point implied team total (23rd).

33. Zach Charbonnet (vs. CHI)

See Jadarian Price above.

34. Mike Washington Jr. (at NYJ)

Jets DT Sweat being out is a big deal.

35. Elijah Mitchell (at WAS)

36. Kenneth Gainwell (vs. ATL) - 24 proj. total yards

37. Samaje Perine (vs. TEN)

38. Chris Rodriguez Jr. (vs. IND) - 29.5 proj. total yards

39. Corey Kiner (at MIA)

40. Justice Hill (at BUF) - 39.5 proj. total yards

41. Tyler Allgeier (at DAL)

Allgeier's legs look heavy to me. It's been that way all year, and it's reached a point where Bam Knight essentially rendered Allgeier a complementary player. He only had eight carries, adding three receptions as the trusted pass protector, per coach LaFleur. He's the RB46 on RB39 usage this year and can be dropped with Jeremiyah Love (ankle) expected to practice and return this week.

The Cowboys defense ranks seventh in half PPR points allowed to opposing backfields at 22.6 per game, giving up top-5 production specifically to ground games with 16.4 rushing points allowed per game (fifth). Opponents have leaned into that tendency, as offenses facing Dallas have a 44% neutral pass rate, the lowest in the NFL. Arizona carries a 24.0-point implied team total (12th) as 6.5-point road underdogs.

42. Emanuel Wilson (vs. CHI)

43. Dylan Sampson (at PIT) - 29.5 proj. total yards

44. MarShawn Lloyd (vs. CAR) - 39.5 proj. total yards
