item.title: NFL odds, betting, storylines: 2 underdogs to back in Week 8
item.description: Let's look at two spots where some 'dogs are in position to bark in Week 8.
item.content:encoded:
Sometimes, less is more. That's not just an overused cliché; it's a solid handicapping strategy.

Which brings me to my NFL underdog best bets for Week 8: After looking over the oddsboard and crunching the numbers on each matchup, there weren't a ton of underdogs screaming out "Bet me!"

So rather than hit you with the usual trio of NFL underdog recommendations, I've streamlined it to just two this week.

In both instances, I'm fading home favorites, which actually has been a pretty sound strategy: So far this season, home teams laying points are 24-35-2 ATS, including 6-15-1 ATS the past three weeks.

Here are my two favorite NFL underdogs wagers for Week 8:

Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets (-1.5)

A month ago, the Raiders were 3-0, and talking heads from coast to coast were left to ponder the question, "Are the Silver & Black really back?" Four consecutive defeats later, and we have our answer: Nope.

I certainly learned that the hard way in Week 7, when I backed Las Vegas against the Rams with one of my underdog best bets. Los Angeles jumped out to a 28-3 lead and cruised to a 35-21 win.

It was the third time during their four-game slide that the Raiders failed to defend their home turf. But look at the opponents: Chiefs, Bills and Rams — three of the top Super Bowl contenders entering this season. And Las Vegas put up a legitimate fight against Kansas City (30-27 loss as a five-point underdog) and Buffalo (33-30 loss as a 5.5-point pup).

The other franchise to take down the Raiders this season was New England. The defending AFC champs rolled Las Vegas 45-17 at home in Week 4. 

Now the Raiders head back to the East Coast. However, for the first time since Week 3, the opponent is the furthest thing from a Super Bowl contender. Rather, it's the Jets, who lost 28-25 at home last week to the previously winless Dolphins. The same Dolphins team that arrived in New York having not held a lead all season.

The Jets, who went off as a 3.5-point favorite against Miami, are now 2-5 this season; 5-19 since the start of last season; and 10-21 since the start of 2024. They're also now 4-8 SU and ATS in their last dozen games as a favorite.

The Raiders, meanwhile, have cashed in five of seven games this year, including four of six when catching points.

Admittedly, Las Vegas' defense has been nonexistent the last five weeks, giving up 35, 30, 45, 33 and 35 points. But the Jets have been held under 20 points four times, and their high-water mark came in last week's loss. The "Gang Green" defense hasn't exactly picked up the slack, either; four of the last five opponents have put up at least 23 points (including one offense led by Tyson Bagent).

Again, the Raiders just endured a brutal four-game gauntlet. This week, I expect them to look more like the team that opened the season by waxing the Dolphins, Chargers and Saints (the latter two on the road).

Bet: Raiders +1.5

Los Angeles Chargers at Los Angeles Rams (-6.5)

Only one NFL team enters Week 7 without a victory. And only one NFL team enters Week 7 without having covered a single point spread. Lo and behold, it's the exact same team: the LA Chargers, who come out of their bye week at 0-6 SU and 0-5-1 ATS.

There is no sugarcoating it: The Chargers, who entered 2026 favored to make the playoffs for a third straight season, have been an abject disaster. And nobody has been more of a disaster than Justin Herbert.

The Chargers' quarterback has the second-worst passer rating in the league. He's thrown three more interceptions (eight) than touchdown passes (five). He's playing behind an offensive line that has been absolutely ravaged by injuries (which is why he's been sacked 21 times, tied for third most in the league). And this week, he faces the NFL's fourth-best pass defense.

And speaking of defense, thanks in part to Herbert's generosity with the football, the Chargers are giving up 25.2 PPG. All six opponents have tallied between 22 and 30 points.

So of course I'm taking the points with the Chargers this week (just as I did in their last game, when they got steamrolled 22-6 in Kansas City).

Call it a careless contrarian move. Or a blindfolded dart throw. Or playing the "due" theory. But I know this much: Two weeks ago, the "unstoppable" Rams lost 18-16 at home to the Cardinals as a 12.5-point favorite. And while they looked sharp last week in Las Vegas, the overwhelming preseason Super Bowl favorites are still under .500 and have yet to win consecutive games this year.

Bet the Los Angeles Chargers to cover the spread at sportsbooks

Also, if you include three playoff contests, the Rams are mired in a 4-8 ATS slump. Not once in those 12 games have they covered the spread in back-to-back weeks.

Meanwhile, in their first two seasons under Jim Harbaugh, the Chargers went 2-0 SU and ATS following a bye. And as pathetic as this franchise has been historically, it has not failed to cover a spread in seven straight games since going 0-7-1 ATS from Weeks 7-14 in … 2001.

Bet: Chargers +6.5

item.description: Our NFL handicappers give out their favorite bets for Week 8 games.
item.content:encoded:
Week 8 of the NFL season began with the Green Bay Packers getting back on track with a 27-19 home win over the Carolina Panthers on Thursday night.

What will the rest of the weekend have in store for bettors?

Our NFL handicapping team of Matt Jacob, Jeremy Pond and Matt Russell combine to give their best bets for Week 8 of the NFL season.

Odds subject to change.

Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3.5, 46.5)

Jacob: I'm not going to call the Minnesota Vikings a fraud — that's a bit harsh. But let's put it this way: There's a reason as many as 11 teams have shorter Super Bowl odds right now than the only team still undefeated.

Look, you can't argue with an 11-game overall winning streak (and a 6-0 start to this season). Nor can you argue that the Vikings field the NFL's best defense — one that's yielding a scant 12.3 points per game. (The next stingiest defense? Kansas City at 17.2 PPG.)

Here's what's also true, though: Since opening with a pair of divisional victories over Green Bay (despite trailing 22-10 well into the second half) and Chicago (which squandered multiple touchdown opportunities and lost quarterback Caleb Williams on a potential game-winning drive), Minnesota's competition has been weak.

We're talking four straight games against the Buccaneers, Dolphins, Saints and Colts. Combined record: 7-20.

Now, the Vikings travel to the Motor City to face a rejuvenated Lions squad coming off consecutive victories over Arizona (45-21 on the road) and Green Bay (20-17 at home). The most crucial thing to isolate in those two scores? The numbers to the right of the dash. 

After shutting out the Saints in the first half of the season opener, Detroit's defense gave up 127 points in the ensuing 14 quarters. So holding the Cardinals and Packers to 38 total points suggests progress. Things should be even easier for the Lions' stop unit this week, as Minnesota is averaging just 17.2 PPG since Week 2.

Last week, the Vikings came off a bye and barely took out the lowly Colts 16-10 at home. Their previous home game? A touchdown-less 15-10 win over Miami. Translation: This team is long overdue for an "L". And I'm confident Detroit will deliver it Sunday by at least a touchdown.

Bet: Lions -3.5

Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3, 54.5)

Russell: Ray Lewis isn't walking through that door. In fact, a much younger, more effective version of Roquan Smith isn't either, as he's the 34th-ranked linebacker by PFF grade this season, which is still a higher grade than either Ravens cornerback. 

Remove garbage time, fourth downs and turnovers — getting to the root of a team's defensive effectiveness — and Baltimore is 14th in EPA/Play and 19th in Success Rate allowed. That's actually flattering, because when you factor in that the Ravens don't turn opponents over (just three interceptions and three fumble recoveries), the numbers get worse.

The Bills defense isn't any good at all, but that hasn't been an issue for a Josh Allen-led offense that has outscored its opponents in an absurd four wins when they've allowed 30-plus points. 

Coming off a bye, there's been two weeks for development in this transitional season for Buffalo's defense under Jim Leonhard, giving more time for the incremental improvement of a young unit.  

Lamar Jackson is expected to return, and it's possible that -2.5 shows up once that's official, but if he isn't able to go, this line should be north of a touchdown. Given the nature of Jackson's injury and history, the chance of re-injury is higher than usual. Meanwhile, even if he were 100% throughout, the Ravens' market rating is still clinging to dominant first halves against the Colts and Titans, and the assumption that the Ravens offense can go shot-for-shot with Buffalo is too far a reach.

Bet: Bills -3 

New England Patriots (-7, 43.5) at Miami Dolphins

Pond: Drake Maye and the Patriots have had plenty of time to get their heads straight after last week's 30-24 road loss against the Chicago Bears.

And what better way for New England (4-3) to get back in its groove than a cushy matchup against the lowly Miami Dolphins (1-5), who are currently a touchdown underdog heading into this showdown in South Florida.

When it comes to finding his teammates in the end zone, Maye has been on fire of late. He has thrown for 12 touchdowns against just two interceptions in the Patriots' last four outings, including a four-TD effort against the Las Vegas Raiders.

I fully expect Maye to keep this aerial trend going and have another big day. Miami has allowed opposing QBs to complete just under 77% of their passes, so I think Maye should have no issue completing at least two of those for touchdowns.

Bet: QB Drake Maye over 1.5 TD passes (-138, FanDuel)

Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5, 40.5) at Denver Broncos

Jacob: A week ago, I told you the Seahawks' defense would smother former teammate — and NFL leading rusher — Kenneth Walker III. And that's precisely what happened, as Walker was held to a season-low 36 yards on 14 carries in the Chiefs' 20-3 loss to the defending champs. His previous low: 70 yards in Week 3 at Miami.

Now we're jumping back on the Walker bandwagon. My rationale? No different than last week: It's all about the opponent. Only three teams — the Cowboys, Raiders and Saints — have surrendered more rushing yards this season than Denver. On a per-game basis, the Broncos are allowing 133.3 ground yards, which ranks 28th. They're also getting gashed for more than 4.5 yards per carry.

Of course, a big reason for these numbers is Walker. In his Kansas City debut in the Week 1 Monday nighter, Walker gashed Denver for 173 yards on 24 carries in a 31-10 rout. And exactly two years earlier — Week 1 of 2024 — Walker rumbled for 103 yards in helping the Seahawks to a 26-20 victory over the Broncos (who went on to finish with the third-stingiest rush defense).

In addition to Walker, Denver this year has been bowled over by Jacksonville's Bhayshul Tuten (65 yards on just 13 carries); the Rams' Kyren Williams (88 yards, 15 carries); the Chargers' duo of Omarian Hampton and Kimani Vidal (combined 110 yards, 22 carries); and the 49ers' Christian McCaffrey and Debo Samuel (combined 96 yards, 18 carries).

Will the Broncos, still miffed about what happened in Week 1, key in on Walker on Sunday afternoon? Of course. Unlike against Seahawks, though, it won't matter.

Bet: Kenneth Walker III over 82.5 rushing yards

Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Commanders (-5.5, 40.5)

Pond: Two teams headed in the wrong direction square off Sunday night and I think the visiting side has the edge ahead of this affair.

Philadelphia (2-5) continues to watch its playoff hopes fade away, largely in part due to the loss of QB Jalen Hurts. Running back Saquon Barkley is playing hurt, but will likely try to give it a go for this NFC East clash. Wide receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks are both questionable as well, meaning it's slim pickings for quarterback Tanner McKee in regard to pass-catching options.

So why the Eagles? Well, Washington (1-4-1) has just as many problems. QB Jayden Daniels is dealing with an elbow issue, plus RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt and WR Terry McLaurin are both on IR.

This is going to be one of those divisional dogfights, and while both teams are dealing with issues during respective seasons currently on downward spirals, it doesn't mean we won't see a spirited effort.

Back the Eagles to keep this one close despite all the absences and ailing players. I'm also jumping on Makai Lemon at a juicy price to score a touchdown for the second consecutive game. Lemon finished with seven receptions on eight targets for 67 yards and a touchdown against Dallas, and looks ready for a breakout in the second half of the season.

Bets: Eagles alt spread +6.5 (-122) and WR Makai Lemon anytime TD (+340) at FanDuel

item.title: Eagles vs. Commanders is an ugly Sunday Night Football game. Why wasn't it flexed?
item.description: Why didn't the NFL flex the "Sunday Night Football" game between 1-4-1 Washington and 2-5 Philadelphia? Explaining league's "flexible scheduling" guidelines.
item.content:encoded:
On Sunday, Nov. 1, Carrie Underwood is going to try to convince NFL fans she's been waiting all day for a matchup between two teams with a combined three wins. That's an easier sell in Week 3 than it is in Week 8.

The 1-4-1 Washington Commanders are due to host the 2-5 Philadelphia Eagles on "Sunday Night Football" this week. While the NFL had a deadline of Oct. 20 to move a different matchup to occupy the prime-time slot on NBC for Week 8, the league opted to keep things as-is.

There are plenty of other interesting matchups set to kick off earlier in the day on Nov. 1 that might have slotted in nicely to a game broadcast to a national audience. Steelers-Browns is a battle for first place. Chiefs-Broncos is, too. And the Lions-Vikings game is another divisional rival game between two teams with winning records.

EAGLES AT COMMANDERS: Predictions, picks and odds for NFL Week 8 game

Week 8 would not have been the earliest a game has been flexed out of "Sunday Night Football" – but it would have been second-earliest.

In 2018, the NFL flexed a game between the San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams out of prime time in Week 7. At the time, the Rams were undefeated, but the 49ers were 1-4 and missing then-starting quarterback Jimmy Garoppolo.

With precedent for earlier flexes out there and several better matchups for "Sunday Night Football," why is the league sticking with Commanders-Eagles in Week 8? Here's what to know about the league's "flexible scheduling" rules:

NFL flex schedule rules

According to NFL.com, the first iteration of the league's flexible scheduling rules were implemented in 2006 "to promote quality matchups on Sunday nights and give surprise teams a chance to play their way onto primetime."

To avoid scheduling chaos, the league has specific guidelines for when and how often it can flex games into (and out of) prime-time slots. These guidelines differ for the three weekly slots available: "Thursday Night Football," "Sunday Night Football" and "Monday Night Football."

Here's how they look, per NFL.com:

  • Sunday Night Football: Can be flexed up to twice between Weeks 5-10, and any game during Weeks 11-17. The NFL must decide and notify all involved teams of the switch 12 days in advance for Weeks 5-13. After Week 13, the league only needs to notify teams six days in advance.
  • Monday Night Football: Can be flexed any week between Weeks 12-17. As with its Sunday night counterpart, "MNF" flexes require 12 days of notice. Unlike its Sunday night counterpart, that window never shrinks to six days.
  • Thursday Night Football: Can be flexed up to twice between Weeks 13-17. Those decisions must "be made no later than 21 days prior to the game."

WEEK 8 STORYLINES: "Thursday Night Football" could be a showcase for NFL's rising penalty trend

Why didn't the NFL flex 'Sunday Night Football' in Week 8?

According to Rob Tornoe of the Philadelphia Inquirer, the "NFL seriously considered flexing in Browns (5-2) vs. Steelers (5-2) on SNF next week." So why didn't they?

The explanation could come down to the other networks that the league would be getting involved with in any flexing decision. NBC has the rights to "Sunday Night Football," but Fox and CBS split the rights to the rest of the Sunday slates during the NFL season.

Moving a different game to "Sunday Night Football" in Week 8 would mean pushing Commanders-Eagles onto a different network, and the networks have rules about protecting games they initially had rights to broadcast.

According to multiple reports, CBS is entitled to the rights for at least one game in each division rivalry for the 16 AFC teams. Fox is entitled the same for the 16 NFC teams.

The three best matchup options the league might have chosen to flex into "Sunday Night Football" in Week 8 – Vikings at Lions, Chiefs at Broncos, Browns at Steelers – either already had a matchup in prime time (the latter two) or are scheduled for a future game in prime time (Vikings-Lions is "SNF" in Week 15). That means CBS, per reports, needs to be allowed to keep Chiefs-Broncos and Browns-Steelers, while Fox gets to hold onto Vikings-Lions.

Ultimately, the NFL let the Oct. 20 flex deadline for Week 8 pass and, ostensibly, remains in good graces with CBS and Fox – if not NBC, which is stuck with Commanders-Eagles.

item.title: Lions' new uniforms: 'Defend the Den' alternates have carbon-fiber elements evoking Motown
item.description: Team's "Rivalries" uniforms feature subtle details meant to honor Detroit's automotive roots while touting team's home-field advantage.
item.content:encoded:
The Detroit Lions will debut their new alternate uniforms in Week 8, though you might need to be something of an NFL fashion aficionado to notice.

The Lions will wear their Nike "Rivalries" kits − aka their "Defend the Den" uniforms − for the first time in Sunday's critical NFC North matchup with the undefeated Minnesota Vikings (6-0), a game Detroit (4-2) very likely needs to win if it's going to stay in the race for this season's division title. Given the game will take place in Motown at Ford Field, not to mention how the Lions are promoting their new look, they should probably win.

"Detroit was once defined by what it built. Now, it’s defined by what it overcame; by its complete refusal to surrender," the team stated when revealing its alternate unis in August. "That mentality is reflected by its people and its football team, in the way they guard the places they call home.

"Every opponent is an intruder."

Beware to the Viking horde. Otherwise, here's what to know about the Lions' duds:

What's new about the Lions' 'Rivalries' uniforms?

If you're only catching highlights from Sunday's Lions-Vikings game, a quick glance might suggest Detroit is wearing its alternate Honolulu Blue helmets atop its road uniforms. But the Defend the Dens aren't the brilliant white the Lions normally feature away from Michigan, more the slightest shade of gray.

And while the helmets might look almost exactly like the ones they used in last week's last-second win over the Green Bay Packers, the lion logo and centerline stripes will feature a carbon-fiber detailing which "symbolizes elite performance and connects to Detroit’s car and racing culture" − and will also extend to the italicized jersey numbers. The shoulders and pants will have jagged black-and-Honolulu Blue striping elements, "Detroit" is inscribed above the numbers, and "Defend the Den" is stitched inside the collar.

Every opponent is an intruder. pic.twitter.com/LcMzpfIjuu

— Detroit Lions (@Lions) August 25, 2026

What are NFL 'Rivalries' uniforms by Nike?

Think of them as the football version of the sports apparel company’s NBA "City Edition" uniforms or Major League Baseball’s "City Connect" jerseys. Nike has strived to create something that further strengthens NFL teams’ bonds to their unique civic environments. And, as “rivalries” would suggest, all of them will be worn in intra-divisional matchups.

“Rivalries uniforms will celebrate storied local traditions and unite fan communities with designs unique to select cities and teams,” Nike announced during the program’s launch in 2025.

"The designs are rooted extensively in the legacies and inspirations true to each team, serving as authentic, competitive expressions of community pride while giving athletes and fans an opportunity to connect like never before."

Which NFL teams have 'Rivalries' uniforms?

Eventually all of them will. This year, AFC South and NFC North squads are joining the AFC East and NFC West teams that kicked off the initiative last year. Every team that has a “Rivalries” uni is scheduled to wear it once this season. The other four divisions will be added to the rotation over the next two seasons, and the “Rivalries” option then becomes part of a team’s closet for the following three years.

item.content:encoded:
As Week 8 follows on the heels of Halloween, the Atlanta Falcons hope to avoid a house of horrors at Raymond James Stadium in a high-stakes NFC South clash against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. After a 0-4 start, the Bucs’ season looks resurrected with recent wins, and the Falcons hope to end their hopes in a nightmare scenario. But to survive the scares in Tampa Bay, the Falcons will need to summon some supernatural performances from five key players.

Michael Penix

Quarterback Michael Penix Jr. will need to pack his holy water and grip his crucifix tightly as he attempts to exorcise the blitzing demons of Todd Bowles’ defense. The Bucs love to bring the heat, and Penix has shown poise under that extra pressure, posting the 6th-best DVOA according to FTN Fantasy.

However, when those blitzes actually create pressure, the script flips into a horror movie: Penix ranks 31st against pressure per the same source. To banish demonic doubts, Penix must use his quick release to attack the soft spots over the middle before Tampa’s ghoulish pass rushers can drag him down.

Kyle Pitts

While Tampa Bay prepares its haunted house, tight end Kyle Pitts enters Week 8 as their ultimate recurring nightmare. Like a classic horror-movie villain in a hockey mask, no matter how many times the Bucs think they’ve stopped him, Pitts always comes back. In eight career games against Tampa Bay, Pitts has terrorized their defense with six touchdowns while averaging over 78 receiving yards per game.

Considering he averages roughly 40 yards per game against all other opponents and a third of his career touchdowns have come against Tampa Bay, Pitts channels a slasher-flick energy against the Bucs. If he wields the machete again on Sunday, Atlanta’s offense will be in great shape.

Ryan Neuzil

Pitts isn’t the only monster haunting this matchup. The Bucs feature a terrifying creature in 350-pound nose tackle Vita Vea. That places the onus squarely on Falcons center Ryan Neuzil to gather his silver bullets and hold the line against a beast that ravenously devours run plays.

If the Falcons hope to establish the ground game against Tampa Bay’s second-ranked run defense, Neuzil and the interior offensive line will need a heroic, monster-slaying effort.

Gervon Dexter

On the other side of the trenches, defensive tackle Gervon Dexter will need to play the Grim Reaper. The Bucs boast a dangerous rushing attack, and Dexter must help control the line of scrimmage. But his soul-harvesting duties don’t end there, as quarterback Baker Mayfield has also struggled under pressure this season.

If Dexter can help the Falcons’ front collapse the pocket, they can force Mayfield into grave mistakes and collect crucial takeaways just like they did in last week’s win over the San Francisco 49ers.

Kendal Daniels

For the second straight week, rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels will don the green dot to lead the defense in Divine Deablo’s absence. Stepping into the caller’s role, Daniels will have to haunt the A- and B-gaps to help Dexter and the defensive line bury the Bucs’ run game. If the rookie phantom can diagnose plays quickly and fill his assignments without giving up the ghost, Atlanta’s defense will be well-positioned to stop the Buccaneers.

Surviving a road trip to Tampa Bay on Halloween weekend won’t be easy, but the Falcons are well-equipped to pull off another frightful upset. If they can, they’ll take complete control of the NFC South. Can you name any other Falcons that will be tricked or treated in this matchup?

item.title: Miami Dolphins offensive line review: Tracking the guards in Week 7
item.description: A weekly scorecard tracking the development of Dolphin guards Kadyn Proctor and Jonah Savaiinaea.
item.content:encoded:
Do my eyes deceive me, or did the Dolphins just win their first game of the Hafley/Sullivan era? Doing it against the Jets is an added bonus, but while wins and losses matter, much of the focus in 2026 remains on the development of Miami’s young talent.

That is especially true along the offensive line, where rookie left guard Kadyn Proctor and second-year right guard Jonah Savaiinaea are important pieces of the team’s future. How are they performing this season? Each week, we take a closer look at the guards and what is being said about their most recent performance.

Kadyn Proctor

Jonah Savaiinaea

What We Learned

The last time we looked at the guards, we were concerned over Jonah Savaiinaea’s ankle injury. With the extra week of rest, he was fine to play – but now we’re worried about Kadyn Proctor. Proctor has been ruled out for Week 8 against the Patriots due to a concussion, which hurts the team’s efforts to secure their second consecutive win and interrupts Proctor’s development. So far this season, the offensive line has been one of Miami’s biggest strengths, paving the way for five consecutive 100-yard rushing performances, and individually Proctor has yet to surrender a sack through six games. Proctor will likely be replaced by Jarrett Kingston, who filled in admirably during Savaiinaea’s injury in Week 5.

Looking at the two guards’ PFF grades for this week, you wouldn’t think the Dolphins as a team had played especially well. Neither player earned a PFF grade of 60, generally considered league average, despite the Dolphins scoring four offensive touchdowns and controlling the game on the ground when it mattered most. That disconnect speaks to the difference between evaluating individual assignments and evaluating the offense’s overall success.

Grades notwithstanding, the eye test reinforces what we’ve seen so far this year: Proctor is already an offensive force to be reckoned with. Physically, the athletic ability, power, and movement skills are already NFL-caliber: Locked On Dolphins’ Kyle Crabbs called Proctor’s performance against the Jets “his best graded game of the season by a fairly comfortable margin.” There’s still room for growth, but the biggest opportunities are mental: recognizing defensive looks more quickly and becoming more consistent with his assignments.

For Savaiinaea, it seems like he is still making progress and is light years ahead of where he was a year ago, but Proctor’s development appears to be further along at this stage (something the PFF grades would attest). He’s more consistently doing the things you want to see – washing defenders down the line, keeping his feet moving, not getting distracted by unexpected movements by the defense. He still played hesitantly at times against the Jets, which feels normal in the course of offensive line development.

What is very clear on tape is that both Proctor and Savaiinaea were instrumental in Miami’s success on the ground. Time and again, they displaced Jets defenders and created cutback lanes for Ollie Gordon. More importantly, when the Dolphins needed to salt away the game in the fourth quarter, the coaching staff trusted the offensive line to win at the point of attack. That may be the most encouraging sign of all.

The tracker will be updated each week throughout the season. For a more in-depth breakdown of Proctor’s and Savaiinaea’s performance, check out offensive line Coach Eric Smith’s film analysis of the game, which you can find on his YouTube channel, Focused on Fins.

item.title: 5 Questions with Big Cat Country: A New Era?
item.description: In Week 8 of 2026 our Indianapolis Colts will travel to the sunshine state to take on the Jacksonville Jaguars. Knowing the party was hitting the road, I sat down with Gus Logue of Big Cat Country. We swapped questions and answers about both the Jaguars and Colts and what follows is what I’ve learned […]
item.content:encoded:
In Week 8 of 2026 our Indianapolis Colts will travel to the sunshine state to take on the Jacksonville Jaguars. Knowing the party was hitting the road, I sat down with Gus Logue of Big Cat Country. We swapped questions and answers about both the Jaguars and Colts and what follows is what I’ve learned about this week’s enemy.

You can find my answers to his questions here.

Chris Shepherd: How are Jaguars fans feeling about their postseason chances sitting at 4-2 with a firm lead on the AFC South? Is this team a contender or do they just play in the AFCS?

Gus Logue: I don’t think opinions in Jacksonville have changed much since before the season began. Of course, playing in the AFC South is a nice boost, but the Jaguars are clearly a top-10 or so team in the NFL right now. We’re just not yet sure whether this roster has hit its ceiling, which is a good thing, but one thing that could hold Jacksonville back from being a legitimate Super Bowl contender is its trench play. LT Anton Harrison was just lost for the season due to a knee injury, and every Jags fan is clamoring for pass rush help before the trade deadline. 

If the OL and DL can take a jump over the second half of the season, the league should really watch out for Jacksonville — and even if that doesn’t happen, Trevor Lawrence and Travis Hunter could still take this team far.

Chris Shepherd: If you were an offensive coordinator tasked with creating a game plan to beat this Jaguars defense, what would it look like? Anyone you would target? Anyone you would avoid?

Gus Logue: I would target the safety position in general. Antonio Johnson is quietly among Jacksonville’s best defensive players, but he’s been ruled out for Sunday’s game with an ankle injury. No. 2 safety Eric Murray had a concussion a few weeks ago and No. 3 safety Caleb Ransaw is on injured reserve. 

Very few rushers have been able to reach the second level of Jacksonville’s run defense, so in order to attack this undermanned secondary, I would put the ball in my quarterback’s hands and have him attack the middle of the field. Just don’t throw it to #12. 

Chris Shepherd: Who are a couple of lesser known players Colts fans should get ready to see a lot of this Sunday?

Gus Logue: Rookie receiver Josh Cameron has been impressive in limited action thus far this season. Even if Brian Thomas Jr. does not get traded, expect the Jaguars to keep giving Cameron offensive snaps. The Baylor product has been a great glue guy with special teams and run blocking contributions, but he’s also super exciting with the ball in his hands. If you don’t know what folks mean when they say a wideout has “strong hands,” then watch Cameron.  

Kaevon Merriweather and Rayuan Lane III figure to split snaps at safety in Johnson’s absence, but I would also look for cornerback Montaric “Buster” Brown. He parlayed a career season into a new contract early in the offseason, but a hamstring injury has made him look almost unrecognizable. Jags fans will be praying that he is fully recovered coming out of the bye week.

Chris Shepherd: Given a win this weekend Jacksonville will go to 5-2. Do you see a potential for them to make any moves at the trade deadline? What positions might they look to upgrade?

Gus Logue: Perhaps they will add depth at offensive tackle after losing Harrison for the season. The more likely scenario is that Jacksonville upgrades its pass defense. 

The Jaguars have lacked pass rush depth since 2018 (only one year after its historic “Sacksonville” season). For years, the EDGE room has consisted of Josh Hines-Allen, Travon Walker, and a bunch of chumps. And Arik Armstead has been a decent 3-tech but interior push has been lacking for nearly a decade as well. The Jaguars need another pass rusher (Josh Sweat?) to help close out games against elite quarterbacks in January. But I also think that a veteran safety (Jessie Bates?) could fix a lot of communication errors in the secondary, the way Jakobi Meyers stabilized the passing offense last season. 

Chris Shepherd: The Jaguars are heavy favorites at home this weekend. How do you see this one playing out and what will the final score be?

Gus Logue: I see the Jaguars taking care of business and winning by double-digit points. Let’s say 26-13. This is a potential look-ahead spot for Jacksonville, as they will play on Thursday Night Football in Baltimore next week, but they’ll be eager to play at home in new uniforms against a struggling division opponent on Sunday. The Bhayshul Tuten Breakout Game could come this week.

And with that, ladies and gentlemen, our week eight preview with the enemy is in the books. I want to thank Gus Logue for giving us some answers to out questions for this week.

Here’s to an entertaining and injury free game.

As always, go Colts.

item.title: Jets RB Breece Hall not expected to play Sunday vs. Raiders in Week 8
item.description: Breece Hall is expected to miss his fourth consecutive games due to a quadriceps injury, NFL Network reports. Braelon Allen is in line to start again.
item.content:encoded:
The New York Jets are likely to be without starting running back Breece Hall for yet another week.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport says Hall is not expected to play today when the Jets host the Las Vegas Raiders (1 p.m. ET, Fox). Hall has been dealing with a quadriceps injury that has kept him sidelined for the last four games.

Hall practiced on a limited basis this past week, but the Jets apparently wanted to see him go through a full session before putting him back on the field.

Braelon Allen will get the start once again for the Jets.

Allen's recent success in the lead back role may have also played a part in the decision to hold Hall out another week.

In the four games he's started in Hall's place, Allen has averaged 89.3 rushing yards per game. He went for 104 yards on 17 carries and caught a season-high six passes for 30 yards in Week 7 against the Dolphins.

According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, the Jets are hoping to have Hall back for next week's game at Kansas City.

item.title: Two kickers are better than one?
item.description: The Los Angeles Rams are dressing at least two kickers for Week 8 and more NFL news on a Sunday
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Rams may be using two kickers and punter for their Week 8 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers. So, are the Rams then using three kickers? Seems that way.

The Rams will go with Brandon McManus, Joshua Karty and then Ethan Evans as the punter. McManus will likely get the nod for field goals while Karty is maybe possibly expected to handle kickoffs. It’s interesting as the Rams truly are trying anything they can to get the special teams improved. Will it work?

If not, truly what else will the Rams be able to try? Sunday is a big test for the Rams and their much-maligned special teams unit. Sunday is a big test for the Rams in general.

Rams will have 2 kickers vs. Chargers after promoting Joshua Karty (ramswire)

“The Rams have used their activations for special teams in the past, usually for players who operate on the coverage/return teams. This time, the franchise is calling up kicker Joshua Karty and long snapper Jake McQuaide for the contest.

Both players were on the team last season before being added to the practice squad this week. Karty, who was waived after missing multiple field goals and extra-point attempts, has a “knuckleball” kickoff that some in the media have pointed to as a potential solution for the team’s coverage issues. The Rams still have Brandon McManus on their roster, so it’s not clear what Karty’s role will be.“

Sean McVay’s crazy two-kicker gamble might actually be genius (sports.yahoo)

“Even last Sunday against Las Vegas, McManus watched Raiders returners rip off gains of 42 and 39 yards. McVay eventually resorted to asking him to kick the ball through the end zone.

That’s not fixing the problem. That’s surrendering to it.

Enter Karty back through the door he first entered when he was drafted by the Rams in the sixth round of the 2024 NFL Draft. 

The former Rams kicker developed a knuckleball-style kickoff that resembles a soccer free kick, deliberately striking the football with minimal spin to create unpredictable movement.“

Is Puka Nacua Playing Today? (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Chargers vs. Rams in NFL Week 8) (si.com)

“Still, with the Rams down Davante Adams (hamstring), the L.A. offense is going to run through Nacua as long as he can be out on the field.

The star wideout still played in 84.7 percent of the team’s offensive snaps in Week 7, catching eight of his 10 targets for 68 yards and a score. This season, Nacua has 45 catches on 62 targets for 485 yards and two scores in just five games. He’s averaging over 12 targets per game, which gives him an extremely high floor when it comes to the prop market.“

3 Rams veterans who likely won’t be back next season (ramblinfan)

“General manager Les Snead faces a difficult challenge in managing the current roster while setting up the same team to succeed next season. The Rams have more than two dozen pending free agents, many of whom are at risk of not returning. Extension dollars will be limited. Here are three veterans whose return is unlikely.

Rams may have already decided to part ways with these 3 veterans

1. Wide receiver Tutu Atwell

The trade that reunited the Rams with Atwell made little sense when it was announced. It makes even less sense now. Despite limited snaps from Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, and a lack of production from the remaining receivers, Atwell sits on the bench. That’s even more confusing when tight end injuries are factored in.“

3 major storylines ahead of Rams vs. Chargers (sports.yahoo)

“The season is young, but wins in the NFL are scarce. The Green Bay Packers are currently holding down the last wild-card spot after their Thursday night win against the Carolina Panthers, and the Rams host them on Thanksgiving Eve. Just saying.

For the Chargers, it’s even worse. With the trade deadline looming, players and coaches are competing for their livelihoods. Desperation drives the narrative.

Sunday special team scaries

The Rams’ special teams have been a letdown this whole season, and their kick coverage team has been simply awful. Now, the team has brought back kicker Joshua Karty and long-snapper Jake McQuaide on their practice squad, activating them both for this game.“

Rams vs. Chargers Prediction, Odds, Pick For NFL Week 8 (foxsports)

“The Rams lead the NFL in total offense (399.1 yards per game) and are coming off a season-high 35 points against the Raiders.

Matthew Stafford has thrown eight touchdowns against one interception over his last three games, completing 75.9% of his passes with a 113.4 passer rating.

The Chargers are the NFL’s last winless team at 0-6 and lead the league with 15 giveaways.“

Rams defense ready for challenges Justin Herbert presents (ramswire)

“Despite the lack of overall offensive success, Herbert has displayed enough, paired with his defense, to keep games close, prompting the Rams’ defense to focus on stopping him. Defensive coordinator Chris Shula detailed the challenges Herbert presents.

“I see that he’s tall, strong, stands tall in the pocket, tough,” said Shula. He sees the whole field, can activate the whole field. A bunch of playmakers, guys running, disperses it, gets the guys out. You see a really good player. Obviously, I know they’re not exactly where they want to be right now, but you see everything is out there for him to be a great offense.”

Can the Rams replicate a balanced offense against the Chargers? (ocregister)

“The offense as a whole fed off their energy, too, with receivers suddenly finding more room to operate as defenses had to respect the run on play-action calls.

“Being able to get these [defensive backs] to take that extra yard or two up to bite on the run fake and it allows us to play with more grass. The more grass that we have to play with, the more confident No. 9 is in being able to let that one go,” receiver Puka Nacua said. “The confidence that he has in letting the ball go is always at 100 percent, but I think when there’s more grass, it goes past 100.”

Head coach Sean McVay sometimes bristles when asked about “balanced” play calling. He doesn’t want to be locked into running 50% run plays and 50% pass plays just because of the concept of balance.“

Ian Rapoport’s Myles Garrett injury update brings ‘optimism’ (clutchpoints)

““There is optimism that Myles Garrett returns to practice this week. I know there was optimism last week, and much more this week. He should practice and should be on the field playing relatively quickly,” Rapoport wrote on X, formerly Twitter.“

Rams, Chargers on collision course with same problems, on and off the field (usatoday)

“The Los Angeles Chargers are a woeful 0-6. The Los Angeles Rams are a disappointing 3-4. And as the teams head into their game Sunday, Nov. 1 at SoFi Stadium, they’re struggling with another problem.

Both teams are struggling off the field as measured by their fan bases. The Nielsen Scarborough NFL Fandom Index released in August highlights the issue.

Only one in four adults in the Los Angeles market watched, streamed, attended, listened to or followed the Rams in the past year, based on data available when the study was released. That accounted for 24% of the Los Angeles market and left roughly 11 million adults with no connection to the Rams.“
